articles.headline: China confirms trilateral summit between Xi, Trump, and Putin in Shenzhen
articles.title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin summit in Shenzhen on November 19
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping will host a trilateral meeting with United States President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on November 19, 2026, in Shenzhen, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Ministry. The historic gathering is expected to take place alongside Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation talks, though authorities did not specify the agenda items for the leaders.
articles.description: The Chinese Foreign Ministry gave no further details including about what the topics of the historic meeting in the southern Chinese city would be

articles.headline: 70 bodies recovered from Gaza rubble, thousands still missing
articles.title: 70 bodies recovered from Gaza rubble, thousands still missing
articles.description: 70 bodies recovered from Gaza rubble, thousands still missing

articles.headline: Iran launches drone attack targeting US military base in Bahrain
articles.title: Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
articles.summary: Iran launched six drones at the al-Riffa air base in Bahrain, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, marking the second such attempt in three days. Bahrain's military stated that its air defense systems intercepted the attack before it achieved its objectives. The incident occurred amid ongoing tensions between Washington and Tehran concerning shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: It marks the second attack on the country in three days and comes as the US and Iran remain locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh reviews cyclone preparedness as 173 fishing boats remain at sea
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra on November 20; Naidu reviews preparedness, 173 fishing boats yet to return
articles.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu evaluated state readiness on November 16, 2026, as the Bay of Bengal depression prepares to hit the coast as Cyclone Akvan by November 20. Agriculture officials urged farmers to secure 23.87 lakh hectares of crops. Meanwhile, authorities confirmed that 30,635 out of 30,808 fishing vessels returned safely, while search operations continue for the remaining boats.
articles.description: Andhra’s Agriculture Minister asks officials to help farmers harvest ready crops and move produce to safety before Cyclone Akvan

articles.headline: Beijing hails upcoming US, China and Russia summit in Shenzhen
articles.title: Beijing hails ‘groundbreaking significance’ of U.S., China, Russia summit in Shenzhen
articles.summary: China announced that President Xi Jinping will host U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, during the APEC gathering. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning praised the historic trilateral meeting as having groundbreaking significance. Experts note the talks will likely focus on Ukraine and energy supplies despite existing geopolitical tensions.
articles.description: The meeting is likely to be more symbolic than substantial. U.S. officials have indicated that the agenda is the war in Ukraine, the situation in West Asia, including stabilising global energy supplies, and nuclear arms control

articles.headline: Supreme Court grants bail and suspends sentences for two Bilkis Bano case convicts
articles.title: Bilkis Bano case: Supreme Court suspends sentence, grants bail to two convicts
articles.summary: Justices MM Sundresh and P.B. Varale suspended life sentences for Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya on October 28, 2026, noting both men spent over 17 years in prison following the 2002 Gujarat riots. Additional Solicitor General Raja Thakre strongly opposed the decision. The convicts were among eleven individuals whose previous remissions were annulled by the apex court in 2024.
articles.description: "Having heard the parties, it suffices to state that the appellants have been incarcerated for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law," says Supreme Court

articles.headline: International Court of Justice to deliver verdict in Myanmar Rohingya genocide case
articles.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya ‘genocide’: Refugee crisis, timeline of the case, and more
articles.summary: The United Nations court in The Hague will issue a final ruling on November 19, 2026, regarding allegations that Myanmar committed genocide against the stateless Rohingya minority. Gambia initiated the lawsuit in November 2019 under the 1948 Genocide Convention. The landmark case follows decades of sectarian violence, military crackdowns, and mass refugee exoduses into neighboring Bangladesh.
articles.description: The international community is closely watching the top UN court’s Rohingya verdict as an archetype for the case filed by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.

articles.headline: US deploys USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier to the Middle East
articles.title: USS Roosevelt arrives in Middle East: Is the US-Iran war about to resume?
articles.summary: The United States military stationed the nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East by November 15, 2026, bringing the total regional carrier strike groups to three. The deployment occurs while diplomatic negotiations involving Pakistan and Qatar remain stalled following a collapsed memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran earlier this year.
articles.description: The aircraft carrier joins two others operating in the US Central Command area of responsibility.

articles.headline: Russia stalls Ukraine talks with maximalist demands to fracture European security
articles.title: ‘NATO will collapse’: Russia stalls Ukraine talks, seeks to divide Europe
articles.summary: During United States-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, Russian diplomats presented demands that go far beyond a peace settlement, seeking to dismantle Europe's post-Cold War security architecture. According to leaked documents and analysts, Moscow wants the North Atlantic Treaty Organization to withdraw troops from Central and Eastern Europe and sign individual nonaggression pacts that could undermine collective defense.
articles.description: Russia has proposed nonaggression pacts with individual nations, which could shatter collective defence against Moscow.

articles.headline: World Health Organization warns antimicrobial resistance could cause 39 million deaths
articles.title: Antimicrobial resistance could kill 39 million people over 25 years: WHO
articles.summary: The United Nations health agency stated that growing antimicrobial resistance threatens to make routine surgery and childbirth life-threatening if prevention and antibiotic use do not accelerate. Officials noted that drug-resistant infections were directly responsible for more than one million deaths in 2021 and released new diagnostic tools to help countries strengthen laboratory capabilities.
articles.description: UN's health agency says growing resistance to antibiotics and other medicines threatens 'future of modern medicine'.

articles.headline: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East amid tensions with Iran
articles.title: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East amid tensions with Iran
articles.description: Trump shares a message saying: ‘May God protect our troops’ as the USS Theodore Roosevelt arrives in the Middle East.

articles.headline: Ukraine hits Russia's Crimea bridge in 1,300-drone barrage
articles.title: Ukraine hits Russia's Crimea bridge in 1,300-drone barrage
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces launched over thirteen hundred drones targeting Russian territory, successfully striking the Crimea bridge and causing minor damage that led to restricted traffic. Russian-installed governor Sergey Aksyonov confirmed the impact, while Moscow reported numerous interceptions. The aerial assault preceded an upcoming trilateral summit in Shenzhen involving world leaders discussing international security.
articles.description: The strike on the bridge appeared to inflict only minor damage, though drew an angry response from Russian-installed officials

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi travels to Manila for ASEAN and East Asia summits
articles.title: PM Modi arrives in Philippines to attend two key regional summits
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi traveled to Manila in the Philippines on November 16, 2026, to attend the 23rd Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit at the invitation of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. Modi stated that ties with ASEAN form the core of India's Act East Policy. Quad leaders are also scheduled to meet on the sidelines on November 17, 2026, according to a senior United States official.
articles.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is visiting Manila on November 16-17 to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr.

articles.headline: UK, Australia, Canada and Italy urge Israel to allow humanitarian access to Gaza
articles.title: UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza
articles.summary: Foreign ministers from the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Italy issued a joint statement calling on Israel to permit immediate humanitarian access to Gaza, where recent floods have worsened conditions and thousands of tents remain held at the border. The conflict began after a Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, resulting in tens of thousands of deaths during subsequent military operations.
articles.description: The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy say Israeli authorities are holding back vital supplies at the borders, including 150,00 tents.

articles.headline: South Africa police probe two weekend shootings that left 17 dead
articles.title: South Africa police probe two weekend shootings that left 17 dead
articles.summary: South African authorities are investigating two separate mass shootings that resulted in seventeen fatalities over the weekend. Nine victims were discovered inside a shack within an informal settlement in Pretoria, while eight others were found dead inside a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg. Police have not yet established a motive or made any arrests in connection with either incident.
articles.description: The ​motive for the shooting has not ⁠yet been established, and no arrests have been ‌made

articles.headline: China resists a nuclear treaty with the US and Russia
articles.title: Why is China resisting a nuclear treaty with the US and Russia?
articles.summary: Beijing remains hesitant to join any trilateral nuclear arms control treaty with the United States and Russia due to a significant disparity in warhead numbers. While Washington and Moscow possess thousands of weapons, China maintains a smaller, rapidly growing stockpile of approximately six hundred twenty warheads. Chinese officials emphasize their minimum deterrence posture and cite previous US withdrawals from key arms pacts.
articles.description: Beijing has a smaller arsenal than Washington and Moscow and worries that a pact could limit its nuclear capabilities.

articles.headline: Ousted Bangladesh PM Hasina vows to return home in December
articles.title: Ex-Bangladesh PM Hasina says if death is the price to pay for returning home, she is ready to face it
articles.summary: Ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina stated she will return home in December despite facing a death sentence and numerous legal charges following her removal from power. Living in exile in India since fleeing a student-led uprising, she rejected the legitimacy of her trial and criticized Bangladeshi authorities for issuing threats instead of facilitating her voluntary repatriation.
articles.description: She was sentenced to death in absentia last year after a Bangladeshi court convicted her of crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on protesters

articles.headline: Yemeni forces withdraw from Bab al-Mandab Strait leaving Houthis in control
articles.title: Yemeni forces' retreat leaves Houthis in control of key area on coast of Red Sea waterway
articles.summary: Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia withdrew from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait on November 15, 2026, leaving the waterway under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement. The military redeployed troops to defend the interim capital of Aden. The seizure of the strait disrupted global oil exports and escalated a conflict that has displaced nearly 330,000 people, according to United Nations estimates cited in the report.
articles.description: Saudi-backed forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the interim capital Aden.

articles.headline: Wholesale prices rise 12.29% year-on-year in October across India
articles.title: Wholesale inflation surges to 12.29% in October, fuel and power prices lead rise
articles.summary: Government data released on November 16, 2026, showed that wholesale inflation quickened to 12.29% year-on-year in October, surpassing the previous month's rate of 11.39% and economists' average forecast of 12.1%. The increase was driven by higher prices across sectors, with fuel and power recording a sharp surge of 32.84% compared to the previous year.
articles.description: According to provisional government data, inflation in the fuel and power category climbed to 32.84%, while primary articles recorded inflation of 9.24%. Inflation in manufactured products, meanwhile, eased marginally to 9.54%

articles.headline: Prince and Princess of Wales arrive in India for official visit
articles.title: Prince and Princess of Wales arrive in India ahead of meeting with Modi
articles.summary: The Prince and Princess of Wales have travelled to India for a three-day official visit, marking their first international trip together in four years. During the tour, Prince William and Catherine will attend events related to the Earthshot Prize and meet Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday to strengthen diplomatic ties between the nations.
articles.description: Most of the engagements the royal couple will attend are related to the Earthshot Prize, which Prince William founded.

articles.headline: Odisha orders early evacuation of vulnerable areas as cyclone approaches
articles.title: Odisha orders early evacuation of vulnerable areas as cyclone threat looms
articles.summary: The Odisha government directed district administrations on November 16, 2026, to begin early evacuations in southern regions as a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal intensified. The India Meteorological Department warns the system could strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm, reaching the Andhra Pradesh coast by November 19 and bringing heavy rainfall to Odisha.
articles.description: The weather system is likely to develop into a very severe cyclonic storm before reaching the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19 night

articles.headline: Russia's Andreeva defeats Ukraine's Svitolina to win WTA Finals
articles.title: Russia’s Andreeva defeats Ukraine’s Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win WTA Finals
articles.summary: Russian tennis player Mirra Andreeva captured her first Women's Tennis Association Finals title by defeating Ukrainian rival Elina Svitolina in straight sets in California. The match concluded without the traditional handshake, adhering to established Ukrainian policy. Andreeva earned millions and a luxury car, while Svitolina announced plans to return to Ukraine to support ongoing relief efforts.
articles.description: Mirra Andreeva won the final in straight sets to end her first Grand Slam-winning year as world number two.

articles.headline: Five European Union nations to unveil Rwanda migrant deportation hub deal
articles.title: European Union nations to unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
articles.summary: Five European Union nations including Germany and Denmark will announce an agreement on November 16, 2026, to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda. The pilot hub aims to host about one hundred people and facilitate repatriations. Human Rights Watch criticized the plan, citing concerns over Rwanda's human rights record, while officials hope the facility will be operational in 2027.
articles.description: The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a so-called "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the EU cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules

articles.headline: Global powers race to replace outgoing United Nations chief Antonio Guterres
articles.title: US and rivals spar over next UN boss as race lurches towards deadline
articles.summary: The race to replace outgoing United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is entering its final weeks ahead of a December 31 deadline. Eight candidates are competing amid geopolitical rivalries and opaque processes. Costa Rican diplomat Rebeca Grynspan leads recent straw polls, though potential vetoes from permanent Security Council members pose hurdles to securing the position.
articles.description: Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan is the current frontrunner, polls suggest, but the US and Russia could veto her bid.

articles.headline: Estonia to close Russian border crossings following suspected sabotage attack
articles.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after attempted arson attack
articles.summary: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia starting December 1, 2026, according to Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna. The decision follows the detention of eight suspects over an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems, which Tallinn blamed on Russian military intelligence. Moscow dismissed the accusations as another demonstration of Russophobia.
articles.description: Estonian authorities detained ‌eight people overnight on suspicion of an attempted arson attack on ‌drone maker Threod Systems that they ‌said ⁠had been ordered by Russia’s ⁠GRU military intelligence service

articles.headline: US proposed Ukraine cede Donbas parts for NATO membership
articles.title: US suggested Ukraine cede parts of Donbas to Russia to become part of NATO
articles.summary: United States negotiators suggested that Ukraine surrender parts of eastern Donbas in exchange for joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Speaking in remarks released on Saturday, Zelenskyy stated he refused to cede territory but indicated he would hold a national referendum if comprehensive security guarantees and reconstruction funds were provided by international partners.
articles.description: Zelenskyy rejected the possibility of Ukraine committing to neutrality and said he refused to cede territory to Russia.

articles.headline: Trump considers holding off on further attacks against Iran
articles.title: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations, sources say
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump has told advisers that he may delay further military action against Iran if Tehran and its allies commit no new provocations, according to three sources. Regional leaders including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan urged the president during phone calls to avoid escalating the conflict further.
articles.description: The war has hiked global fuel prices and proven unpopular with U.S. voters, who handed control ‌of ⁠Congress to the Democrats in last week's midterm elections

articles.headline: England defeat Spain 3-2 to secure top spot in group A3
articles.title: England stun Spain 3-2 to end record unbeaten streak
articles.summary: England defeated world champions Spain 3-2 in Madrid on November 16, 2026, ending La Roja's record forty-four match unbeaten run in competitive games. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White secured the victory, while Spain responded through Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams. England finished as group winners in Nations League group A3 despite playing with ten men following Elliot Anderson's second-half red card, according to the report.
articles.description: Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja's first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat

articles.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak remains out of control six months into response
articles.title: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo six months into response
articles.summary: Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, government data shows over eleven thousand cases and nearly half of those infected have died. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, eighty percent of new cases are detected outside health surveillance. Children and frontline workers face severe risks amid conflict and attacks in eastern provinces.
articles.description: The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016

articles.headline: World Health Organisation warns of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza
articles.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
articles.summary: The World Health Organisation reported that acute respiratory infections in Gaza have risen by 33,000 cases compared to last year. Dr Reinhilde Van De Weerdt stated that heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians, worsening overcrowding and living conditions. The agency warned that the situation will deteriorate further during winter, while Israeli military agencies maintained that winterisation supplies and medical equipment have been facilitated into the region.
articles.description: Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher

articles.headline: India health expenditure triples as household out-of-pocket spending declines
articles.title: India’s health spending triples to ₹4.14 lakh crore, but out-of-pocket share drops to 42.7%: NHA
articles.summary: India's Union government health expenditure increased from ₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013-2014 to ₹4.14 lakh crore in 2023-2024, according to National Health Accounts estimates. The Health Ministry reported that the proportion of out-of-pocket spending by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over the decade. The data highlights expanded public financing, increased primary healthcare spending, and growth in government and private health insurance schemes across the country.
articles.description: The share of healthcare costs borne by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over a decade, while social security spending on health rose from 6% to 11%

articles.headline: Mirra Andreeva defeats Elina Svitolina to claim WTA Finals title
articles.title: Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina to win WTA Finals; ascends to No. 2 in rankings
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old Russian tennis player Mirra Andreeva defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 on November 15, 2026, to win the WTA Finals without dropping a set at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Andreeva earned 3.37 million dollars and a Mercedes-Benz convertible, rising to number two in the world rankings. Svitolina collected 1.5 million dollars after finishing as the runner-up in the eight-day tournament, according to the match report.
articles.description: The WTA Finals win helped Mirra Andreeva to clinch her career-high ranking, just behing Elena Rybakina

articles.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week
articles.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin plan to hold a trilateral meeting next week during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, according to White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales. The leaders of the world's largest nuclear powers will discuss reducing nuclear weapons and the war in Iran, while bilateral talks are also scheduled between Trump and Xi.
articles.description: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.

articles.headline: Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if U.S. trade talks fail
articles.title: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated in Cambodia on November 16, 2026, that Canada could pursue alternative partnerships with Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with United States President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. Carney emphasized that Washington talks remain his priority following a January agreement that permitted limited Chinese electric vehicles into Canada under reduced tariffs.
articles.description: Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts

articles.headline: Protests erupt in Gopalganj over proposed return of ousted leader Hasina
articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.summary: Supporters of ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina staged violent demonstrations in Gopalganj on November 15, 2026, demanding her return from India. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia in November 2025 for crimes against humanity. The unrest prompted the government to withdraw local officials and deploy paramilitary forces to maintain public order.
articles.description: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

articles.headline: US government seeks 24-year prison term for Nikhil Gupta
articles.title: U.S. govt seeks 24-year prison term for Nikhil Gupta in Pannun murder-for-hire plot
articles.summary: United States authorities are pushing for a 24-year prison sentence for Indian national Nikhil Gupta over his involvement in a foiled plot to assassinate American citizen Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. Gupta previously pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire charges and is scheduled to be sentenced on November 20 by United States District Judge Victor Marrero.
articles.description: Gupta will be sentenced on November 20. His lawyers have, however, argued for a "substantial downward" sentence of 12 years' imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release

articles.headline: Nvidia must hire outside chief executive after Huang departure, Bessent says
articles.title: U.S. Treasury chief Scott Bessent wants answers soon from Nvidia
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Nvidia must hire an outside chief executive following the resignation of Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down on November 12, 2026, amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Bessent added that the board and outside counsel must answer questions regarding export compliance within 10 days.
articles.description: U.S. Treasury ‌Secretary Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge U.S. restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China

articles.headline: Houthis advance in Yemen as government forces move to defend Aden
articles.title: Houthis advance in Yemen as government forces move to defend Aden
articles.description: An advance by the Houthi armed group in Yemen is threatening one of the government’s last strongholds.

articles.headline: Megaspeed launches internal investigation into business and supply chain
articles.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
articles.summary: Singapore-based Megaspeed announced an internal investigation into its business operations after executive Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy linked to Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang, left her role in August 2025. The company stated it complies with all regulatory regimes, while US treasury and commerce officials face mounting congressional scrutiny over high-end AI chip exports.
articles.description: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.

articles.headline: US aviation authorities investigate nationwide ground stop caused by equipment failure
articles.title: After a nationwide ground stop, US faces aviation infrastructure questions
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration grounded United States flights for nearly four hours following a router malfunction during an upgrade performed by defence contractor L3Harris. Over 9,000 flights were cancelled and 1.5 million passengers stranded. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that investigations are ongoing into the incident, which has also renewed scrutiny regarding ageing infrastructure across the national aviation system.
articles.description: Trump has requested $50bn for upgrades, but Democratic lawmakers are asking for transparency before spending more.

articles.headline: India offers extended service terms to military recruits under Agnipath scheme
articles.title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?
articles.summary: India's Ministry of Defence announced on 4 November that soldiers finishing four-year terms under the Agnipath programme can serve two additional years at higher pay. Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani stated the decision followed internal reviews. More than 18,300 recruits will complete their initial tenure by the end of 2026, amid ongoing debates regarding training duration and military effectiveness.
articles.description: India has softened its recruitment scheme, giving young soldiers a longer military stint and another shot at permanent service.

articles.headline: US proposes Ukraine cedes territory for NATO membership, says Zelensky
articles.title: U.S. proposes Ukraine cede territory in exchange for joining NATO: Zelensky
articles.summary: United States officials suggested for the first time that Ukraine should cede land to Russia in exchange for joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Moscow rejected an energy target ceasefire during talks in Abu Dhabi. He emphasized that any decision regarding territorial concessions would require societal approval following confirmation of security guarantees.
articles.description: Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had rejected a ceasefire on energy targets at talks in Abu Dhabi, as Moscow was “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold trilateral meeting at APEC summit
articles.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting at APEC: What to expect
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin will participate in their first trilateral meeting during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Discussions will primarily address nuclear proliferation, notably the expired New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty. The gathering also occurs amid ongoing geopolitical tensions concerning conflicts in Ukraine and Iran alongside bilateral trade disputes.
articles.description: A nuclear treaty and the US's war on Iran are among priority topics for China, Russia and US leaders.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces withdraw from Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden
articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces announced a strategic withdrawal from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait area to prioritize the defense of Aden. The retreat on November 15, 2026, marks the end of a six-week counteroffensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, who previously seized the Red Sea coast. Meanwhile, the International Committee of the Red Cross reported that the Houthis released 600 prisoners on the same day amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

articles.headline: Thousands of US flights face cancellations following technical failure
articles.title: Thousands of US flights still cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
articles.summary: Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed after a technical failure in a communication router caused a national ground stop. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy stated normal operations may take time to recover as aircraft remain out of position. President Donald Trump urged Congress to approve funding to modernise the system.
articles.description: The US transport secretary says that normal air-traffic operations may not be restored until Monday.

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot calls for Benjamin Netanyahu's removal amid alleged election meddling
articles.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu can’t remain Israel PM amid alleged vote meddling
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot demanded the immediate departure of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following allegations of electoral interference reported by broadcaster Channel 12 on Sunday. The report claimed Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, improperly prompted police raids against Ra'am party members before the October 27 election. Netanyahu's Likud party condemned the remarks as outrageous incitement.
articles.description: Arab party members were reportedly arrested before Israeli elections based on unfounded evidence from the PM's office.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strike kills three in Russia amid NATO territory claims
articles.title: Three killed in Russia as Ukraine claims US floated NATO membership option
articles.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack killed a family of three in the Russian border region of Belgorod, according to local authorities. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed that United States negotiators raised the possibility of ceding eastern territory for North Atlantic Treaty Organization membership during recent talks in Abu Dhabi, though Kyiv rejected any immediate withdrawal from the Donbas region.
articles.description: Zelenskyy says the US asked for the first time whether Kyiv would cede land to Moscow in exchange for the NATO bid.

articles.headline: US media implicates former Indian intelligence chief in Pannun plot
articles.title: U.S. media names Indian official who allegedly ordered plot on Gurpatwant Singh Pannun
articles.summary: United States authorities assessed that an alleged assassination plot against Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun was directed by the former chief of India's Research and Analysis Wing, Samant Goel. According to a report by the Washington Post, officials believe the operation received official sanction from individuals connected to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs declined to comment on the allegations.
articles.description: According to Washington Post, R&AW official Vikash Yadav directed businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic, to hire a hitman to kill Pannun outside his New York residence; it says NSA Ajit Doval was ‘probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists’

articles.headline: Four nations urge Israel to allow immediate humanitarian aid into Gaza
articles.title: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow aid into Gaza
articles.summary: Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom urged Israel to permit immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza following severe floods. The foreign ministers noted that 150,000 tents and vital supplies remain restricted at the border. More than 1.9 million people have been displaced in the territory during the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: The countries accuse Israel of preventing tents and other supplies from entering Gaza, despite the humanitarian crisis.

articles.headline: Bessent calls for outsider leadership at Nvidia following executive scandal
articles.title: US Treasury chief calls for outsider to lead embattled tech firm Nvidia
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advocated for external leadership at Nvidia during a television appearance on November 15, 2026. The technology firm faces scrutiny after former chief executive Jensen Huang resigned following reports of an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence. Bessent also called for a 10-day deadline to verify export compliance.
articles.description: Scott Bessent gives Nvidia's board 10 days to show the company's compliance with US export controls.

articles.headline: Israel restricts aid entry as winter storms batter Gaza
articles.title: Who can force Israel to implement Gaza ceasefire deal?
articles.summary: Palestinians in Gaza face harsh winter weather in tents without basic services while Israel restricts humanitarian aid entry. Calls from the United Nations, European Union and the US-established Board of Peace have gone unanswered, leaving displaced families vulnerable to flooding and cold conditions, according to the report.
articles.description: Storms batter Palestinian territory as Israel restricts entry of aid.

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo remains uncontrolled
articles.title: Africa CDC says Ebola outbreak in DR Congo ‘still not under control’

articles.headline: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis
articles.title: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas commander in Gaza
articles.summary: Hamas confirmed that Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis was killed in an Israeli air strike on al-Mawasi in southern Gaza on November 14, 2026. The strike on a tent sheltering displaced people wounded two others. According to Gaza Ministry of Health figures, Israeli attacks have killed 16 people over a forty-eight hour period amidst ongoing hostilities.
articles.description: Hamas confirms the death of Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis in an attack on Khan Younis on Saturday.

articles.headline: SpaceX captures Starship spacecraft with launchpad arms in Texas
articles.title: SpaceX’s Starship captured by launchpad arms in dramatic first
articles.summary: SpaceX successfully caught its Starship spacecraft using giant mechanical arms at Launch Pad 2 in Texas following a 22-hour flight. While NASA praised the milestone for future Moon missions, the company fell short of a double catch when the first-stage booster exploded after liftoff. The upper stage successfully released 26 advanced Starlink satellites into orbit during the 15th flight.
articles.description: SpaceX officials say catch by mechanical arms shows Starship's full reusability, crucial for rapid, low-cost recycling.

articles.headline: Judo champion Teddy Riner launches surprise French presidential campaign
articles.title: Judo champion shakes up French presidential race with surprise candidacy
articles.summary: Teddy Riner, a heavyweight judo champion holding five Olympic golds, has announced a surprise candidacy for the French presidency next April. Operating without a political party or manifesto, the Guadeloupe-born athlete is positioning himself in the centre against extremism. Pundits note his high popularity could disrupt the existing political field ahead of the upcoming election.
articles.description: Teddy Riner is one of the most popular figures in modern-day France, and one in five voters say they could support him.

articles.headline: Iraq PM targets powerful militia stronghold in $30m oil smuggling probe
articles.title: Iraq PM targets powerful militia stronghold in $30m oil smuggling probe
articles.description: Iraq’s PM has dismissed nine senior security officials over an alleged oil smuggling network worth up to $30m monthly.

articles.headline: Car bomb explosion in Damascus suburb kills child and another person
articles.title: Bomb rips through Damascus suburb; killing 2, including child
articles.summary: An explosive device planted inside a car in Jaramana, a southern suburb of Damascus, detonated on Saturday evening, killing two people including a child and wounding at least one more. According to the Interior Ministry, security forces have cordoned off the site near a battery factory and launched an investigation following the attack amid ongoing security tensions in Syria.
articles.description: The explosion took place in the southern Damascus suburb of Jaramana near a factory where batteries are produced, state TV said

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu calls for national unity government to secure Israel
articles.title: Netanyahu says only a unity government can guarantee Israel’s security
articles.summary: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu urged rival Gadi Eisenkot to form a national unity government to counter Iran. Eisenkot rejected the proposal as a political ploy and stated Netanyahu lost the election. Following the October 27 election where neither bloc won a majority, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government within 28 days.
articles.description: Eisenkot, in charge of forming a government, dismisses the appeal as ‘tricks’ as talks and a Knesset speaker vote loom.

articles.headline: Seventeen people killed in two separate mass shootings across South Africa
articles.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
articles.summary: South African police launched a manhunt after eight men were shot dead inside a minibus in KwaZulu-Nation province and nine people were killed in a shack in western Pretoria during Sunday night incidents. Police stated the shootings are unrelated as the nation continues to struggle with high rates of violent crime and illegal firearms.
articles.description: The shootings in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng highlight South Africa's struggle to curb violent crime.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh government proposes Investment Protection Act to shield business investments
articles.title: Andhra’s proposed Investment Protection Act seeks to shield investors from policy U-turns
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government is planning to enact the Investment Protection Act to prevent policy reversals and safeguard capital from political changes, following past controversies involving renewable energy power purchase agreements and capital shifts. Legal experts and industry leaders noted that the unprecedented legislation aims to restore investor confidence and protect economic planning across the State.
articles.description: The proposed law aims to shield investments from policy reversals by successive governments, such as the ‘three capitals’ plan and the review of power purchase agreements

articles.headline: Security forces engage suspected terrorists during ongoing Kulgam search operation
articles.title: Encounter breaks out in Kulgam during anti-terror operation
articles.summary: An encounter started in Kulgam on November 16, 2026, as security forces continued an anti-terror operation spanning six days. Police stated the area was cordoned off following initial reports suggesting individuals linked to a November 11 attack on the Central Reserve Police Force were trapped. The operation matters as authorities attempt to neutralize militants responsible for prior injuries to security personnel.
articles.description: Initial reports suggested that those involved in the November 11 attack on CRPF may be trapped at the encounter site

articles.headline: Every Chhath, the same question returns: Why is the Yamuna still polluted?
articles.title: Every Chhath, the same question returns: Why is the Yamuna still polluted?
articles.description: Every year during Chhath Puja, images of devotees standing amid toxic foam bring the Yamuna’s pollution crisis back into focus. Despite decades of court interventions, government plans and cleanup projects, the river remains heavily polluted as it passes through Delhi. Experts say the key challenge is not just increasing river flow, but stopping untreated sewage and waste from entering the river in the first place.

articles.headline: United Nations delegates debate potential regulations for lethal autonomous weapons
articles.title: UN-backed talks consider possible rules on lethal autonomous weapons
articles.summary: Government envoys met in Geneva at a United Nations review conference on November 16, 2026, to consider launching negotiations for rules on killer robots. While seven nations proposed a legally binding agreement, Russian officials stated that discussions remain premature. The debate is critical as military powers and international leaders clash over artificial intelligence in warfare and the necessity of human accountability.
articles.description: Scary would-be scenarios, like armed drones flying amok and gunning down civilians with pinpoint precision, have peppered years of discussions about killer robots, but those talks haven't produced any international restrictions

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department forecasts heavy rainfall across Telangana due to Cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan may bring rains to Telangana between November 19 and 21
articles.summary: Cyclone Akvan is expected to bring heavy rain to parts of Telangana between November 19 and November 21, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department. Authorities issued orange alerts for four districts on November 20 and November 21. The weather system matters because severe cyclonic conditions threaten widespread thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds across multiple regional districts.
articles.description: The impact may be observed from Thursday (November 19, 2026). Four district were placed under orange alert, indicating heavy to very heavy rainfall, on Friday (November 20, 2026)

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department issues heavy rain warning for south Bengal districts
articles.title: IMD warns of heavy rain in four south Bengal districts from November 19
articles.summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm, bringing heavy rain to south Bengal districts between November 19 and November 21, 2026. The India Meteorological Department advised fishermen to avoid the sea. This severe weather threatens South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, and Jhargram with thunderstorms and gusty winds.
articles.description: The weather system, which lies over the southeast Bay of Bengal as a deep depression, is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by November 16 evening and subsequently into a severe cyclonic storm as it moves in a north-northwestward direction, says IMD

articles.headline: China and Southeast Asian leaders commit to avoiding South China Sea disputes
articles.title: China, Southeast Asia pledge to avoid disputes during talks on South China Sea pact
articles.summary: China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations pledged on November 16, 2026, to avoid actions escalating South China Sea disputes during annual talks in Manila. Chinese Premier Li Qiang and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. discussed progress on a code of conduct. The talks matter because territorial standoffs in the vital trade route remain a major regional flashpoint.
articles.description: China, Taiwan and four ASEAN states — Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam — have been involved in the decades-long territorial standoffs in the busy waterway, a key global trade route

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu pastoralists demand representation in state wildlife conservation
articles.title: Why Tamil Nadu’s pastoralists are demanding a voice in wildlife conservation?
articles.summary: Traditional pastoral communities in Tamil Nadu are demanding representation in the State Board for Wildlife following its reconstitution by the government on October 28, 2026. The Tamil Nadu Federation of Pastoral Peoples Sangams argues that excluding indigenous herders who possess vital traditional ecological knowledge threatens livelihoods and contravenes existing legal frameworks protecting historical grazing rights.
articles.description: Tamil Nadu government issued a Government Order on October 28, 2026, to reconstitute its State Board for Wildlife—headed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. Missing from the move was representation for traditional pastoral communities.

articles.headline: US negotiators propose Ukraine ceding Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership
articles.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
articles.summary: United States negotiators suggested that Ukraine withdraw remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for North Atlantic Treaty Organization membership during recent talks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated the proposal was raised by American envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff following meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, noting it brought the military alliance back onto the agenda.
articles.description: The US has not confirmed the Ukrainian president's comments - a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed".

articles.headline: Cyclone Akvan approaches Andhra Pradesh coast as IMD issues warning
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to cross Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni by November 20 noon, says IMD
articles.summary: According to the India Meteorological Department, Cyclone Akvan is projected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni as a very severe cyclonic storm by November 20 noon. Winds could reach 145 kmph. Officials have placed district administrations on high alert, suspended offshore operations, and instructed fishermen to remain ashore until November 20 due to dangerous conditions.
articles.description: Andhra fishermen still awaiting compensation for Cyclone Arnab’s losses are told to stay ashore till November 20 ahead of Akvan

articles.headline: Congress and INDIA bloc plan strong alternative in Uttar Pradesh
articles.title: Congress, INDIA bloc will provide strong alternative in Uttar Pradesh, says Kharge
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge stated on November 16, 2026, that his party and the INDIA bloc will provide a strong alternative for Uttar Pradesh in the upcoming assembly polls. Following a strategic meeting in Delhi, leaders emphasized social justice and defeating the Bharatiya Janata Party, amid discussions regarding seat-sharing arrangements with Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav.
articles.description: The upcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh will give a new direction to the country's politics, Mallikarjun Kharge said.

articles.headline: Fishing trawler capsizes in Andaman Sea with many feared dead
articles.title: The tragedy of recurring Rohingya refugee deaths
articles.summary: A fishing trawler carrying between 250 and 280 Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals capsized in the Andaman Sea in mid-April 2026 while attempting to reach Malaysia from Cox’s Bazar. According to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and the International Organization for Migration, approximately 250 people are feared dead or missing, with only nine to ten survivors rescued.
articles.description: The capsizing of a fishing trawler carrying refugees draws attention to the cost of protracted displacement

articles.headline: Rohingya crisis overview and regional displacement issues
articles.title: For Rohingya, there is no place called home
articles.summary: Rohingya Muslims originating from Rakhine state in Myanmar face systemic statelessness under the 1982 Burmese citizenship law and have experienced recurring sectarian violence and military crackdowns. Over recent years, tens of thousands have fled across borders into Bangladesh and India, prompting major humanitarian concerns, security challenges, and ongoing legal and political debates regarding deportation and refugee status.
articles.description: Rejected by the country they were born in and shunned by the neighbouring states, the Rohingya are among the the most vulnerable amongst forcibly displaced groups.

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues warning over Aadhaar face authentication accessibility issues
articles.title: Supreme Court warns contempt if authorities fail to give detailed reply to plea on visually impaired unable to do Aadhaar face authentication
articles.summary: The Supreme Court warned of contempt action if authorities fail to provide a detailed response to an application by advocate Amar Jain concerning visually impaired individuals unable to complete Aadhaar face authentication. The plea highlights e-KYC failures and challenges a mandatory biometric LPG refill order issued by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in October 2026.
articles.description: The Supreme Court issued notice on application pointing out that the inability to complete Aadhaar face authentication was affecting e-KYC, which only relies on face authentication

articles.headline: Belur residents protest following two fatal elephant attacks within three days
articles.title: Elephant attack: Protesters want Forest Minister visit Belur after two deaths in three days
articles.summary: Protesters in Belur blocked a road on November 16, 2026, demanding a permanent solution to human-elephant conflicts after two fatal attacks occurred within three days in Karnataka. Local resident Jayamma was killed on November 14, followed by Hafees Ur Rahman on November 16. Former minister B. Shivaramu criticized the district administration, while Hassan district authorities planned a visit to address safety concerns.
articles.description: The Minister in charge of Hassan district, K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, was expected to visit the spot later in the day along with senior officers

articles.headline: Bahrain court sentences sixty-four Shia individuals to life in prison
articles.title: Bahrain sentences 64 Shias, mostly clerics, to life on terror charges: rights group
articles.summary: A Bahraini criminal court sentenced 64 Shia Muslims, including 57 clerics, to life imprisonment on November 16, 2026, amid an ongoing crackdown on suspected Iran-linked networks. The Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy reported the sentences, while rights groups raised serious concerns regarding alleged torture, forced confessions, and the widespread persecution of religious clerics.
articles.description: Bahrain, a Sunni Muslim kingdom, has a large Shia population that has long complained of marginalisation

articles.headline: Jordanian authorities ban Telegram messaging application over national security concerns
articles.title: Jordan bans Telegram over national security concerns
articles.summary: Jordanian authorities banned the Telegram messaging application on November 16, 2026, citing efforts to curb illegal content and extremist material following a church shooting in Karak. The Public Security Directorate announced the security measure as part of a broader crackdown. Telegram was founded in 2013 by Pavel Durov, who currently faces international investigations and legal scrutiny.
articles.description: The measure comes amid a security crackdown after last month's deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox church.

articles.headline: SpaceX catches top stage of Starship rocket returning to Earth
articles.title: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
articles.summary: SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket using mechanical arms at a Texas launch site. Although the company intended to retrieve both sections, the booster stage experienced an aborted descent and burst into flames over the ocean. The upper section successfully returned on November 14, 2026, marking a historic first recovery.
articles.description: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".

articles.headline: Sadiq Khan: Global North must take responsibility for climate change
articles.title: Sadiq Khan: Global North must take responsibility for climate change
articles.description: At COP31, Sadiq Khan urges wealthy nations to support the Global South, which bears the brunt of climate change.

articles.headline: HRCP warns of escalating threats to democracy and constitutional rights in Pakistan
articles.title: Pakistan human rights body warns of escalating threats to democracy and fundamental freedoms
articles.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan raised concerns on November 16, 2026, regarding an escalating assault on constitutional democracy, judicial independence, and freedom of expression. Following its annual general meeting, the commission highlighted the sentencing of lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Chattha, criticized recent constitutional amendments, and demanded the protection of minorities and fundamental freedoms nationwide.
articles.description: According to a press release issued by HRCP, the commission's General Body expressed alarm over the systematic erosion of freedom of expression through censorship, surveillance, restrictive regulations and the misuse of criminal laws

articles.headline: Prince Harry visits Ukraine to support injured war veterans and Invictus athletes
articles.title: 'You're going to win the war': Harry praises war veterans on surprise Ukraine visit
articles.summary: The Duke of Sussex undertook a two-day surprise visit to Lviv, Ukraine, to meet injured service personnel and Ukrainian competitors participating in the Invictus Games. Prince Harry visited rehabilitation facilities including the Superhumans Center, where he observed advanced medical treatments and praised the resilience of wounded veterans facing ongoing missile attacks from Russian forces.
articles.description: He has been showing support for injured veterans in Ukraine and praising the country's resilience.

articles.headline: Supreme Court upholds Maharashtra reservation rotation policy for local bodies
articles.title: Supreme Court rejects plea against Maharashtra's rotation policy for reserved SC/ST seats in local bodies
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed an appeal challenging Maharashtra government rules that treat general elections following their enforcement as the first for rotating reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in local bodies. Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana ruled that voters do not possess a vested right to specific seat reservations, concluding that the policy falls entirely within government domain.
articles.description: A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana dismissed an appeal filed by Sau. Rupali Indrabhushan Sonde against the September 19, 2025, judgment of the Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court, saying, "No voter or a candidate can have a vested right to have a constituency declared as a reserved seat for SCs or STs”

articles.headline: Sudanese army drone strike kills fifteen civilians in West Kordofan
articles.title: Sudan Army strike kills 15, including children says rights group, survivor
articles.summary: A double-tap drone strike conducted by the Sudanese Army in the village of Abu Qalb killed fifteen people, including four children playing football, according to a survivor and a local rights monitor. The attack occurred during a military counter-offensive against the Rapid Support Forces, escalating a conflict that has triggered severe humanitarian crises across the region.
articles.description: The double-tap strike on November 15 in the village of Abu Qalb also “injured others and burned a number of homes”, reported local rights monitor the Kordofan Observatory

articles.headline: US envoy Kushner aims to broker direct peace talks between Europe and Russia
articles.title: US envoy Kushner says he aims to broker Europe-Russia talks on Ukraine
articles.summary: United States envoy Jared Kushner announced he is working with Russia, Ukraine, and European nations to advance peace negotiations. Speaking on Saturday, Kushner noted that both sides recognize compromises are necessary. The diplomatic push follows recent talks in Abu Dhabi and coincides with European leaders agreeing to send representatives to future discussions.
articles.description: Europe's direct engagement with Moscow as part of Ukraine-Russia peace talks is edging closer to becoming a reality.

articles.headline: Kachin: where Myanmar’s rare earth minerals are in tight grip
articles.title: Kachin: where Myanmar’s rare earth minerals are in tight grip
articles.description: In Myanmar’s northern state of Kachin lies millions of dollars worth of rare earth minerals.

articles.headline: Ahmad Tibi elected deputy speaker of Israel parliament following electoral gains
articles.title: Ahmad Tibi elected deputy speaker of Israel’s Knesset
articles.summary: Joint List alliance chairman Ahmad Tibi was elected deputy speaker of the Israeli Knesset on November 16, 2026, following historic electoral gains by parties representing Palestinian citizens. Tibi called for a criminal investigation into Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding alleged interference in the parliamentary elections, emphasizing that no individual is above the law.
articles.description: Leader of alliance representing Palestinian citizens of Israel says election is 'rightful achievement' for Joint List.

articles.headline: Odisha miners leave 40% of iron ore capacity underutilised amid rising demand
articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.summary: Miners in Odisha left nearly forty percent of approved iron ore capacity unutilised, prompting judicial concern regarding resource waste and potential state revenue losses. While courts highlighted delays and financial impacts, industry sources attributed the low operational rates to lengthy forest clearance procedures affecting production across major mineral-producing states.
articles.description: The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

articles.headline: Over 2,000 people cross over from Senegal into Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.title: Over 2,000 people cross over from Senegal into Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.description: Around 2,000 migrants have crossed into Spain’s Canary Islands from Senegal in two days.

articles.headline: Cruise ship passengers rescued following collision in New Orleans
articles.title: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
articles.summary: Approximately 130 people aboard the American Heritage cruise ship were rescued after a collision with the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday. Thirty-two individuals sustained non-critical injuries and were hospitalised, while no people remained unaccounted for. Officials including Mayor Helena Moreno hailed the successful rescue operation as a miracle on the Mississippi.
articles.description: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.

articles.headline: European militaries seek domestic alternatives to reduce defense technology dependence
articles.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as Militaries seek to limit U.S. dependence
articles.summary: European defense ministries are actively pursuing domestic software solutions to reduce reliance on American technology provider Palantir Technologies for critical military functions. Countries including France, Germany, and the Netherlands are exploring alternative suppliers to ensure national data sovereignty, balancing strategic autonomy against the operational capabilities provided by established U.S. platforms.
articles.description: Last week, Germany’s Helsing unveiled ​military intelligence software called Clarity, which is a part of a broader market for AI-powered systems designed to accelerate military decision-making

articles.headline: Ecuadoran president denies United States military presence following reported aircraft deployment
articles.title: Ecuador’s president denies existence of US military base
articles.summary: Ecuadoran President Daniel Noboa denied the existence of a United States military base near Guayaquil, stating that American personnel at Taura Air Base were participating solely in temporary cooperative activities. The denial followed journalistic investigations documenting unusual aircraft deployments and military flights, which raised domestic legal questions regarding bilateral anti-narcotics efforts.
articles.description: Daniel Noboa says US personnel in the country for 'temporary activities'.

articles.headline: India’s Assam state demolishes homes of 132 Muslim families
articles.title: India’s Assam state demolishes homes of 132 Muslim families
articles.description: Authorities in India’s Assam have demolished the homes of 132 Muslim families.

articles.headline: Pakistan nominates climate minister to represent government at New Delhi forum
articles.title: Pakistan’s participation in SCO Civilisational Forum | Explained
articles.summary: Pakistan designated Climate Change and Coordination Minister Musadik Masud Malik to represent its government at the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue in New Delhi. The event aims to connect ancient civilizations among member countries, bringing attention to Pakistani representation despite ongoing regional diplomatic tensions involving bilateral water treaties and security disputes.
articles.description: The Ministry of Culture, in collaboration with the Ministry of External Affairs, will organise the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum from November 20-22 at the Purana Qila (Old Fort) in New Delhi

articles.headline: Italy fines Meta record €805 million over unauthorised gallery access
articles.title: Why Italy hit Meta with record €805 million fine | Explained
articles.summary: Italy’s data protection authority penalized Meta €805 million on November 14, 2026, for collecting user photos and videos from Android galleries without explicit consent. The platform feature allowed browsing suggestions using device media. This represents the largest monetary penalty ever levied by Italian authorities against a major technology corporation, highlighting growing regulatory scrutiny over digital privacy practices.
articles.description: Italy’s data protection authority conducted a technical analysis after it received a complaint from a consumer protection forum, which said that the platform accessed “unpublished files stored on users’ smartphones”

articles.headline: Phuket commercial shophouse fire kills 11 people and injures 16
articles.title: 11 killed, 17 injured in fire at Phuket shophouse
articles.summary: An early morning blaze on November 16, 2026, destroyed a commercial shophouse in a resort town on Thailand's Phuket island, resulting in eleven fatalities and sixteen injuries. Local law enforcement reported that the fire erupted in a vehicle rental establishment before spreading to adjacent structures near Patong beach. Thai authorities extinguished the flames within two hours, while investigators continue determining the precise origin of the disaster.
articles.description: Police said officers are still investigating the cause of the fire, but initial investigations found an electrical transformer near the building had exploded shortly before the fire started

articles.headline: Kerala Police link arrest to synagogue arson case investigation
articles.title: Kerala Police find similarities between Gurumurthy, Kochi synagogue arson cases; yet to find evidence of Lawrence Bishnoi links
articles.summary: State Police Chief Ravada A. Chandrasekhar stated on November 16, 2026, that investigators identified modus operandi similarities between suspect Gurumurthy and Ebin P. Paul, who is in custody for an October 12 arson attack on the Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Ernakulam. Although both suspects allegedly maintained criminal network ties, authorities have confirmed no direct connection to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.
articles.description: Thrissur police are investigating case against Tamil Nadu native Gurumurthy who was arrested recently from Palakkad for alleged links with criminal networks, while NIA has taken over probe into arson case

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs status reports on special NDPS courts
articles.title: Supreme Court asks Centre, States to file status reports on setting up of special courts to hear NDPS Act cases
articles.summary: The Supreme Court instructed the Centre, states, and union territories on November 16, 2026, to submit fresh progress reports regarding the creation of 449 designated courts to handle Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act cases. A Bench consisting of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana reviewed the backlog and emphasized establishing adequate infrastructure for expeditious trials.
articles.description: Supreme Court took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that not much progress has been made in pursuance of the orders passed by the apex court recently on setting up of special courts

articles.headline: Yellow Vest demonstrations draw over 100,000 people across France
articles.title: More than 100,000 rally across France in new Yellow Vest protests
articles.summary: Demonstrators gathered in multiple French cities for cost-of-living rallies organized by the Yellow Vests and youth movements. The Ministry of the Interior reported 106,000 participants nationwide, while student unions claimed higher figures. Protesters opposed living costs and educational standards, leading to clashes with police in cities like Marseille and Lyon, ahead of further strikes planned by unions.
articles.description: Protesters chant against declining affordability, the Macron government, police violence, and poor school conditions.

articles.headline: Commercial building fire in Phuket kills at least eleven people
articles.title: At least 11 killed in blaze on Thailand’s Phuket island
articles.summary: A fierce blaze in Patong on November 16, 2026, resulted in eleven deaths and sixteen injuries following an apparent electrical transformer explosion. Phuket Governor Chodnarin Koedsom reported that stored motorbikes, gas, and tyres inside a rental shop accelerated the flames. Fifteen Thai nationals and one Myanmar citizen received hospital treatment, while authorities confirmed no tourists were harmed.
articles.description: Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire, which also injured 16, but have ruled out arson.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh survey reveals millions of hypertension and diabetes cases
articles.title: Andhra NCD survey finds 59.63 lakh hypertension, 48.95 lakh diabetes cases
articles.summary: Officials submitted the Non-Communicable Diseases 4.0 survey findings to Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav on November 15, 2026, covering 4.2 crore tested individuals. The assessment identified 59.63 lakh hypertension cases and 48.95 lakh diabetes cases across the state. Additionally, screenings confirmed thousands of oral, breast, and cervical cancer diagnoses, with older demographics recording the highest prevalence of lifestyle diseases.
articles.description: Andhra Pradesh has 59.63 lakh hypertension and 48.95 lakh diabetes cases; 34 lakh people have both hypertension and diabetes

articles.headline: Depression over Bay of Bengal expected to become severe cyclonic storm
articles.title: No rainfall alerts for Andhra as depression to turn severe cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal by November 17
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported that a low-pressure area over the Southeast Bay of Bengal intensified into a depression on November 15, 2026. Currently located hundreds of kilometres from Port Blair and Chennai, the system is projected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17. Authorities in Andhra Pradesh have not yet issued rainfall alerts for the system.
articles.description: At 5.30 a.m., the system lay centred over southeast and southwest Bay of Bengal, about 700 km west-southwest of Port Blair

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department forecasts heavy rain for coastal Andhra Pradesh from upcoming cyclone
articles.title: Cyclone may bring isolated heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh from November 18 to 20
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department forecasted heavy rainfall and gusty winds reaching up to fifty kilometers per hour for coastal Andhra Pradesh from November 18 to 20. A low-pressure system over the southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by November 16, prompting authorities to advise fishermen to return to the coasts by November 15 due to rough sea conditions.
articles.description: According to the IMD’s afternoon bulletin, heavy rain is likely at one or two places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and gusty winds, with speed reaching 40-50 kmph, on November 18, 19 and 20.

articles.headline: Bay of Bengal depression projected to intensify into severe cyclonic storm
articles.title: Depression likely to become cyclone, move towards A.P.; Tamil Nadu, Odisha to get rain: IMD
articles.summary: The meteorological department announced on November 15, 2026, that a depression over the Bay of Bengal will likely intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17. Rain is expected in northern Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal, following rainfall recorded in districts including Chengalpattu, Chennai, Kancheepuram, and Kanyakumari over the preceding 24 hours.
articles.description: If Cyclone Akvan, as the storm is being called, makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh, it will be the third cyclone within a month to hit the State

articles.headline: Low-pressure area forms over southeast Bay of Bengal
articles.title: Low-pressure area forms over Bay of Bengal, likely to intensify into depression by November 15
articles.summary: A low-pressure area has formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal and is expected to intensify into a depression by November 15, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department. The system developed under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation and is predicted to bring squally weather and strong winds to the Andaman Sea and surrounding regions.
articles.description: The system formed at 5:30 a.m. under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the central Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman and Nicobar Islands, according to the latest weather update

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government withdraws six hundred cases against farmers and teachers
articles.title: Tamil Nadu government withdraws 600 cases against farmers and teachers
articles.summary: Authorities in Tamil Nadu issued orders on November 16, 2026, to drop six hundred protest-related cases filed against ninety-two thousand farmers and teachers between May 2021 and April 2026. According to an official release, the move follows a suo motu announcement made by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the Assembly on September 2, 2026.
articles.description: The orders follow Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s suo motu announcement in the Assembly on September 2, 2026

articles.headline: PDP criticises six-day security restrictions in south Kashmir's Kulgam
articles.title: Six days of restrictions in Kulgam reminiscent of 1990s, people facing collective hardships: PDP's Sartaj Madani
articles.summary: Opposition Peoples Democratic Party leader Sartaj Madani condemned a six-day anti-terror operation in Kulgam on November 16, 2026, stating that movement restrictions in Akhran created fear and hardship. Restrictions were imposed after a November 11 attack on a Central Reserve Police Force checkpoint. Madani also criticised the ruling National Conference for remaining silent on civilian difficulties.
articles.description: Parts of south Kashmir’s Kulgam were placed under restrictions following a terrorist attack on a CRPF checkpoint at Akhran

articles.headline: Jay Shah reappointed unopposed as International Cricket Council chairman
articles.title: Jay Shah reappointed as ICC Chairman for second term
articles.summary: The International Cricket Council announced on November 16, 2026, that thirty-eight-year-old Jay Shah was reappointed unopposed for a second two-year term. The decision was finalised during board meetings ending November 15, 2026, to provide leadership continuity as cricket prepares for its return to the Olympics at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
articles.description: Jay Shah took over in December 2024 and was reappointed during the global body's Board Meetings that ended in Bali

articles.headline: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi promises social security for Telangana gig workers
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi promises social security, insurance cover for gig workers in Telangana
articles.summary: During an event in Telangana on November 14, 2026, Indian National Congress leader Rahul Gandhi announced five lakh rupees in accident insurance and ten lakh rupees in health insurance for platform-based workers. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Labour Minister Vivek Venkataswamy were also present as the government introduced legislation to establish dedicated Wi-Fi rest zones and a one percent transaction contribution mechanism directed toward worker welfare.
articles.description: Mr Gandhi said every gig worker would receive ₹5 lakh in accident insurance and ₹10 lakh in health insurance. A social security contribution mechanism under which 1% of every transaction, including deliveries and cab rides, would be contributed towards the workers’ future security

articles.headline: Rising job cuts and tech layoffs spark debate over employee reskilling responsibilities
articles.title: Layoffs and retrenchment: why 15 days’ wages is not enough for employee reskilling
articles.summary: Following significant workforce reductions by companies such as Tata Consultancy Services, which cut approximately 23,000 net jobs by March 2026, technology professionals face growing job insecurity. As global tech layoffs reached about 1.22 lakh and India's attrition rate climbed to 18% in 2026, desk-job employees are increasingly funding their own reskilling certifications amidst a broader economic downturn.
articles.description: Reskilling has become the default answer to a layoff. Amid prevalent instability, few ask the lawyer’s question: is reskilling the individual’s responsibility or a collective one?

articles.headline: US blames outdated technology for nationwide flight disruption
articles.title: US blames outdated technology for nationwide flight disruption
