articles.description: US blames outdated technology for nationwide flight disruption

articles.headline: United States reverses cuts to fund United Nations military support in Somalia
articles.title: In reversal, U.S. to fund UN military support in Somalia for another year
articles.summary: The United States State Department announced on November 15, 2026, that it will renew funding for United Nations and African Union military support missions in Somalia for another year. The reversal cancels planned shutdowns and aims to prevent regional security crises, following Washington cuts driven by frustration with local political instability and Al-Shabaab insurgents.
articles.description: The Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab has been fighting the Somali government for two decades and continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite the African Union military campaign, which was unlikely to be able to continue without UNSOS support.

articles.headline: Italy fines Meta 805 million euros over photo access
articles.title: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
articles.summary: Italy's Data Protection Authority has penalized technology company Meta 805 million euros for accessing Android users' photographs and videos without proper consent through a Facebook app feature. The regulator stated that approximately 20 million individuals were affected by the practice and gave the corporation 60 days to disable the feature by default.
articles.description: The social media giant is accused of not informing 20 million users it had access to their photos.

articles.headline: Prince William and Princess Catherine arrive in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize
articles.title: Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize 2026: All you need to know
articles.summary: Britain's Prince William and Princess Catherine arrived in Mumbai on November 17, 2026, for a three-day visit hosting the sixth edition of The Earthshot Prize. Marking the royal couple's first joint overseas trip since 2024, the event brings together five thousand guests to celebrate environmental innovators competing across five distinct categories.
articles.description: The sixth Earthshot Prize, founded by Britain’s Prince William to promote innovative climate change solutions, will be presented in Mumbai on November 17, 2026

articles.headline: Congress demands independent SIT reporting to Supreme Court over temple donations
articles.title: Ram temple donation theft: Congress seeks new SIT reporting exclusively to Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress party demanded a new, independent Special Investigation Team reporting directly to the Supreme Court of India to investigate the Ram temple donation theft in Ayodhya. Speaking on November 16, 2026, party officials criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi and alleged that government authorities attempted to shield individuals associated with the ruling political establishment by misleading both the public and the judiciary regarding the ongoing inquiries.
articles.description: Congress said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “silence” on the issue is “deeply troubling” to the nation and asserted that those who have betrayed people’s faith must be held accountable

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh prepares for third consecutive tropical cyclone
articles.title: After Arnab and Murasu, Andhra Pradesh braces for another cyclonic storm
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh is bracing for another severe cyclonic storm expected to make landfall along the northern coast on November 19 or 20, following earlier impacts from Cyclones Arnab and Murasu. The India Meteorological Department stated that a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is intensifying, prompting advisories for fishermen to return to shore and coastal residents to remain alert.
articles.description: Cyclone may make landfall along the North Coastal Andhra Pradesh either on the night of November 19 or in the early hours of November 20, says IMD

articles.headline: Rajasthan holds final phase of panchayat polls across 25 districts
articles.title: Voting underway for final phase of panchayat polls in Rajasthan
articles.summary: Elections for the fourth and final phase of panch and sarpanch posts commenced across 3,747 gram panchayats in 25 districts of Rajasthan on November 16, 2026. Over 1.05 crore eligible voters participated at 11,905 polling stations starting at 7 a.m. Voting concluded at 6 p.m., with ballot counting for ward panch seats and sarpanch positions scheduled to begin immediately afterward.
articles.description: More than 1.05 crore voters are eligible to exercise their franchise at 11,905 polling stations. Long queues of voters were seen at several polling stations since morning

articles.headline: Police detain activists before Israel technology event in Hyderabad
articles.title: SIO activists detained in pre-dawn swoop before Israel-T-Hub event in Hyderabad
articles.summary: Mir Chowk police detained members of the Students Islamic Organisation of India during a pre-dawn operation following opposition to a delegation of Israeli companies visiting T-Hub in Hyderabad. The technology incubator event aims to foster business collaborations, though local activists and rights organisations have raised serious concerns regarding military links.
articles.description: Incidentally, the Israeli delegation’s visit and the collaboration does not show up on the schedule of T-Hub, while the schedule is reported in tech-websites.

articles.headline: US blames telecommunications system upgrade for FAA ground stop
articles.title: US blames system upgrade for longest nationwide FAA ground stop since 9/11
articles.summary: United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop to routine maintenance performed by contractor L3Harris on Friday to upgrade an antiquated telecommunications router from copper to fibre. Speaking in Washington, DC, Duffy stated that a faulty router or contractor error caused severe communication disruptions, though officials ruled out any cyberattack.
articles.description: Sean Duffy, the country's transportation secretary, said his agency is 'going to hold people accountable'.

articles.headline: India and Egypt target twelve billion dollars in bilateral trade
articles.title: India, Egypt discuss steps to boost trade, address non-tariff barriers
articles.summary: India and Egypt agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore a preferential or free trade agreement aiming to nearly double bilateral commerce to twelve billion dollars. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and Egyptian Minister Mohamed Farid Saleh co-chaired the Joint Trade Committee meeting in Cairo on November 15, 2026, where both nations discussed reducing non-tariff barriers, enhancing market access, and strengthening manufacturing investments across multiple priority sectors.
articles.description: The two countries have decided to set up a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a PTA or FTA to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries

articles.headline: Martine Moise registers as candidate for Haiti presidential election
articles.title: Widow of Haiti’s slain leader Moise to contest presidential vote
articles.summary: Martine Moise, widow of assassinated Haitian President Jovenel Moise, registered as a candidate for the presidential election scheduled for July 2027. Her candidacy follows years of repeated delays driven by severe gang violence and political instability that have displaced 1.5 million people and caused over 22,000 deaths. She joins thirty-two other registered candidates, including former presidents and prime ministers, as international forces assist local authorities in combating armed groups.
articles.description: Martine Moise is one of ​33 registered candidates running in Haiti's first presidential election in a decade.

articles.headline: Karnataka government notifies amended BMLTA Act to protect infrastructure projects
articles.title: BMLTA Amendment notified: Tunnel Roads, Elevated Corridors to evade institutional scrutiny
articles.summary: The Karnataka government notified the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority Amendment Act on October 9, 2026, retrospectively shielding urban transport projects initiated between 2022 and mid-2026 from institutional scrutiny. Passed during the August monsoon session without debate, the legislation incorporates a controversial savings clause that exempts initiatives like tunnel roads and elevated corridors from the transport planning authority, drawing sharp criticism and pending legal challenges from civic groups.
articles.description: The provision of the Section retrospectively validates decisions and actions relating to projects initiated between the adoption of the BMLTA Act in 2022 and the notification of the 2026 Rules, deeming them to have been undertaken under the Act

articles.headline: Mumbai youth linked to Lawrence Bishnoi gang arrested for reconnaissance
articles.title: Youth held for recce of Jewish establishments was recruited by suspected Bishnoi gang associate arrested in Keralam: police
articles.summary: Mumbai resident Yash Singh was arrested by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad for conducting reconnaissance of Jewish establishments, including the Chabad House. Transferred to Kerala police custody on November 15, 2026, Singh was allegedly recruited by Gurumoorthi, a suspected associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang previously arrested in Ottapalam. Investigators are also probing potential connections between this case and a recent synagogue-adjacent arson incident investigated by the National Investigation Agency.
articles.description: Yash Singh (20), a native of Navi Mumbai, was arrested by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) for allegedly conducting reconnaissance of Jewish establishments, including Chabad House in Mumbai

articles.headline: India faces sustainability challenges amid massive global rice exports
articles.title: Rebalancing India’s Rice economy: exports, virtual water, emissions and the groundwater challenge
articles.summary: India produced 154.02 million tonnes of rice in the 2025-26 period, maintaining its position as the world's largest exporter with shipments totaling 21.57 million tonnes worth $11.54 billion. Experts from the Institute for Social and Economic Change and the International Rice Research Institute argue that policymakers must address heavy groundwater depletion, virtual water trade, and greenhouse gas emissions.
articles.description: India has proved its competitiveness in global rice markets and the next challenge is to make that competitiveness sustainable; the country’s rice policy needs a more differentiated production strategy that moves from volume to value: more crop per drop, more income per tonne, and less energy use per unit exported

articles.headline: Stock markets rebound in early trade driven by foreign fund inflows
articles.title: Stock markets rally in early trade led by foreign fund inflows, lower crude oil
articles.summary: Indian equity benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rebounded in early trade on November 16, 2026, driven by sustained foreign fund inflows and lower crude oil prices. The BSE Sensex climbed 414.36 points, while the NSE Nifty rallied 102.10 points. According to experts, strong capital inflows and better-than-expected corporate earnings growth support this market outperformance.
articles.description: The 30-share BSE Sensex climbed 414.36 points to 82,010.15 in early trade and the 50-share NSE Nifty rallied 102.10 points to 25,252.50

articles.headline: Martine Moise registers as a presidential candidate in Haiti
articles.title: Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election
articles.summary: Martine Moise, the widow of assassinated former Haitian president Jovenel Moise, registered as a presidential candidate for upcoming elections in the Caribbean nation. She was injured in the 2021 attack that killed her husband. Haiti has faced chronic gang violence and instability, with elections postponed until July due to insecurity according to officials.
articles.description: There has not been an election in Haiti since before the death of Jovenel Moise in 2021.

articles.headline: Pakistani minister to visit India for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation dialogue
articles.title: Amidst Indus water tensions, Pakistan to send vocal critic to SCO Civilisational Dialogue; first Ministerial visit in three years
articles.summary: Pakistan Climate Minister Musadik Masood Malik will travel to New Delhi to represent his country at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilizational Dialogue scheduled from November 20 to November 22, 2026. According to the Pakistan Foreign Ministry, this marks the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in over three years, following former Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari's trip in May 2023.
articles.description: Dr. Malik, the Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, had earlier this year said that Pakistan would ‘cut off those hands’ that are trying to control the Indus waters

articles.headline: Secretary of State Marco Rubio addresses economic struggles and foreign policy
articles.title: Rubio acknowledges ’people are struggling’ economically in speech after GOP midterm wipeout
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged economic hardships during a November 2026 speech to the Federalist Society, attributing public frustration to costs. He defended policies like the Iran conflict and criticized international organizations. The remarks follow Republican midterm losses, highlighting ongoing political debates over economic pressures and national sovereignty.
articles.description: Marco Rubio’s comments to the conservative Federalist Society touched on a core issue of the midterm elections — economic pain — that U.S. voters cited in delivering massive losses to Republican Party

articles.headline: Kataib Hezbollah denies involvement in oil smuggling in Iraq
articles.title: Iraqi armed group denies involvement in oil smuggling, calls probe a ‘lie’
articles.summary: The Iran-aligned armed faction Kataib Hezbollah denied involvement in an oil smuggling operation in Iraq's Jurf al-Nasr area. The denial followed an anticorruption crackdown where Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior officials. The group accused the prime minister's office of fabricating lies under pressure from Washington, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.
articles.description: Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah says the group is subjected to 'blackmail' to force disarmament amid US pressure on Iraq.

articles.headline: Megaspeed confirms Alice Huang left executive role last year
articles.title: Megaspeed, firm at centre of Nvidia scandal, says Alice Huang left in 2025
articles.summary: Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed confirmed that tech executive Alice Huang departed her executive role on August 30, 2025. The company faces scrutiny over United States export controls concerning Nvidia graphics processing units. Singaporean authorities are investigating Megaspeed for suspected false declarations, and the Ministry of Home Affairs barred Huang from re-entering the country.
articles.description: Chinese tech executive romantically linked to ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left in August 2025, Singapore-based firm says.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh secures major investments at Visakhapatnam summit
articles.title: A.P. attracts major investments at CII summit in Visakhapatnam
articles.summary: State-owned Hindustan Shipyard Limited and Cyient DLM signed an agreement at the 31st Confederation of Indian Industry Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam to manufacture indigenous marine systems. Meanwhile, Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited and fabrIQ Private Limited committed 43,700 crore rupees for infrastructure and green energy projects across the region.
articles.description: HSL-Cyient DLM pact to boost indigenous marine electronics; MEIL and fabrIQ commit ₹43,700 crore to projects expected to generate over 1.06 lakh jobs

articles.headline: India supports UN General Assembly resolution on Palestinian natural resources
articles.title: India supports UNGA resolution on permanent sovereignty of Palestinian people
articles.summary: On November 11, 2026, the United Nation General Assembly adopted a resolution reaffirming the permanent sovereignty of the Palestinian population and the inhabitants of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources. India joined one hundred fifty nations in voting for the text proposed by Uruguay, which demands that Israel cease resource exploitation, infrastructure destruction, and environmental damage in the affected territories.
articles.description: It demanded that Israel “cease the exploitation, damage, cause of loss or depletion and endangerment of the natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and in the occupied Syrian Golan

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi claims India is no longer a democracy under BJP
articles.title: India is no longer functioning as a democracy, destroyed since 2014: Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: During the Bharat Summit hosted by the Telangana government on November 14, 2026, Lok Sabha Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that India is no longer a democracy. Speaking in Hyderabad, he claimed elections lack legitimacy because the Election Commission allegedly declared fourteen crore voters illegal, and he also alleged that foreign delegates were barred from attending.
articles.description: At the Bharat Summit, the LoP says money power, institutional capture changed the political landscape, left Opposition in shock for a decade; cites anomalies in Maharashtra elections

articles.headline: Italy fines Meta 805 million euros over user photo privacy
articles.title: Italy fines Meta $880m over photo privacy
articles.summary: Garante, the Italian data privacy authority, fined Meta 805 million euros for collecting smartphone users' photographs and metadata via a Facebook application feature without adequate consent. The regulator noted that roughly 20 million Italian Android users may have been impacted by the default setting and cited a lack of cooperation from the company.
articles.description: Regulator said Meta's 'lack of cooperation' and the large number of people affected contributed to size of the fine.

articles.headline: Myanmar airstrike kills 12 at displacement camp in Rakhine state
articles.title: Myanmar airstrike kills 12 at displacement camp in Rakhine state
articles.description: A Myanmar military airstrike on a displacement camp in Rakhine state killed 12 people.

articles.headline: Indonesian president apologises to Singapore and Malaysia for wildfire haze
articles.title: Indonesian president apologises to Singapore, Malaysia for wildfire haze
articles.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto issued a formal apology during the ASEAN summit in Manila regarding severe transboundary haze originating from prolonged domestic wildfires. According to a presidential statement, Jakarta maintains a strict enforcement approach against responsible commercial entities, having revoked seventeen permits and initiated numerous formal investigations. Meanwhile, regional meteorological services recently reported temporary relief from the smoke across affected Southeast Asian territories.
articles.description: Prabowo says his government has a 'zero-tolerance policy' for firms that contribute to blazes and pledges strict action.

articles.headline: Indian grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi eliminated from Total Chess World Championship Tour
articles.title: Tata Chess Pilot: Vaishali defeats Arjun Erigaisi; all three Indians are out of championship race
articles.summary: Indian Grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi missed qualification for the championship knockout stage following a defeat against compatriot R Vaishali during the final group matches in Budapest. Despite early success, Erigaisi placed third in Group D as Maxime Vachier-Lagrave advanced instead. All three Indian competitors failed to reach the main bracket, directing their focus toward upcoming classification encounters against international opponents in their respective playoff brackets.
articles.description: Magnus Carlsen ended the group stage without a win. Carlsen is now down to 2801.2 and in danger of dropping below 2800 for the first time in more than 15 years

articles.headline: European Union urges Israel to grant immediate humanitarian access to Gaza
articles.title: EU calls for immediate humanitarian access to Gaza
articles.summary: The European Union demanded that Israel reopen all Gaza border crossings and allow unimpeded aid delivery following severe flooding that submerged large areas of the territory. The appeal came after an Israeli drone strike killed two Palestinians in Jabaliya and followed an earlier airstrike near the Nasser Medical Complex that resulted in multiple fatalities.
articles.description: The EU said that “Israel must enable the work of the UN and its agencies" after the group was blocked access into Gaza.

articles.headline: Shophouse fire kills at least 11 in Phuket
articles.title: Shophouse fire kills at least 11 in Phuket
articles.description: Fire engulfed buildings in Thailand’s popular tourist town of Patong, killing several people and injuring many others.

articles.headline: New book examines Jawaharlal Nehru through intelligence chief Bhola Nath Mullik
articles.title: Jawaharlal Nehru through an intelligence prism
articles.summary: A recently published analysis explores the professional relationship between India's inaugural Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and his longtime intelligence leader, Bhola Nath Mullik. Mullik directed the Intelligence Bureau from 1950 until shortly following Nehru's passing, operating as the principal authority on national security matters before the establishment of modern external intelligence agencies. The publication highlights a rarely examined operational dimension of the administration.
articles.description: Critics of Jawaharlal Nehru have spared no effort to portray him as being rosy-eyed and naive about China; yet, memoirs of Bhola Nath Mullik, the intelligence chief who served under Nehru for almost the entire duration his Prime Ministership make it clear this was far from the truth

articles.headline: Indian Army troops open fire following suspicious border movement in Poonch
articles.title: Army opens fire after suspicious movement near LoC in J&K’s Poonch
articles.summary: Military personnel deployed along the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir discharged roughly two dozen small arms rounds after detecting suspicious activity within a forest zone. Defense representatives stated that vigilant border guards in the Sawjian sector initiated the tactical response to prevent potential militant infiltration from across the international boundary. A comprehensive search operation commenced at dawn and remains actively underway across the cordoned territory.
articles.description: A search operation was launched with the first light of the day and it was underway when last reports were received, the officials said

articles.headline: Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies in hospital at age 80
articles.title: Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies age 80
articles.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, founder of the Guadalajara Cartel and a pioneer of international drug smuggling alliances, died in a Guadalajara hospital at age 80. Known as The Godfather, he orchestrated partnerships with Colombian cartels during the 1980s cocaine boom. He had remained in state custody since his arrest in 1989 following the murder of Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique Camarena.
articles.description: Known as the 'Boss of Bosses', he was the head of all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s before his arrest broke up his drug organisation.

articles.headline: Quad leaders to meet in Manila for regional security talks
articles.title: Quad Summit likely to be held in Manila on November 17, sources say
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, United States President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will meet in Manila on November 17, 2026, for the first Quad Summit since 2024. Sources in New Delhi confirmed the discussions will focus on critical mineral supply chains and securing commercial shipping lanes amid ongoing maritime attacks.
articles.description: The Summit between leaders of India, U.S., Australia, and Japan is being held in a non-Quad country for the first time, expected to address critical minerals and energy supply chains and safety of seafarers

articles.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines discharged from hospital after car attack
articles.title: Australian MP 'full of gratitude' upon leaving hospital after alleged car attack
articles.summary: Independent Australian politician Helen Haines has left the Alfred Hospital following four weeks of treatment and multiple surgeries after she was allegedly struck by a vehicle outside her Wangaratta office on October 19. Brendan Nugent faces multiple charges regarding the incident, while Victoria Police continue their ongoing investigation into the attack.
articles.description: The MP lost both of her legs after the alleged attack outside her electorate office four weeks ago.

articles.headline: Six-year-old girl goes missing from school in Panchkula district
articles.title: Panchkula school attack: Ringing the school bell, raising a safety alarm
articles.summary: A six-year-old girl went missing from her school in Haryana’s Panchkula district on October 28, 2026. Her school bag was found at the reception area when the auto-rickshaw driver arrived to pick her up. Family members and teachers searched the building before a boy directed her father to a first-floor classroom, where he was told someone had beaten her up, according to the report.
articles.description: A six-year-old girl was allegedly assaulted by an eight-year-old classmate in a classroom in Panchkula, with CCTV footage capturing the attack. The incident raises concerns about school safety, supervision, and the influence of violent video games on children

articles.headline: Odisha signs tripartite agreement for desalination project in Gopalpur
articles.title: Tripartite agreement signed for ₹1,000-crore desalination project in Odisha
articles.summary: The Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation, the International Finance Corporation, and the Odisha government have signed a tripartite agreement for a ₹1,000-crore desalination project in Gopalpur. The public-private partnership initiative will produce 100 million litres of water daily for industries, supporting regional economic development and infrastructure investment goals across the state.
articles.description: Eleven projects worth around ₹15,498 crore, identified as part of the collaboration with IFC, were granted in-principle were approval by State’s Empowered Committee on Infrastructure

articles.headline: ASEAN and China fail to conclude South China Sea code of conduct
articles.title: ASEAN, China fall short of agreeing on South China Sea code
articles.summary: During meetings in Manila, China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations failed to finalize a long-negotiated code of conduct for the South China Sea. Philippine Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro stated that key issues remain unresolved, including whether the agreement will be legally binding. Separately, the bloc extended its ban on Myanmar leaders attending annual summits.
articles.description: Southeast Asian leaders also denounce violence in Myanmar and extend ban on country's leader attending bloc's summits.

articles.headline: Nvidia appoints interim CEO and board chair after Jensen Huang resigns
articles.title: When tech founders leave, what happens to their companies?
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence giant Nvidia has appointed Colette Kress as interim chief executive officer and Harvey Jones as board chair following Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday. Huang stepped down after facing scrutiny from United States lawmakers and shareholders over alleged personal affairs, while analysts warn the departure could significantly impact the company's valuation.
articles.description: Nvidia could lose 30 percent of its value following cofounder Jensen Huang's decision to step down, analysts warns.

articles.headline: SpaceX to attempt double recovery of Starship rocket components
articles.title: Second catch attempt for SpaceX Starship rocket
articles.summary: SpaceX will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Ship upper stage of its Starship rocket using mechanical arms during a test flight on Friday. The mission aims to demonstrate full reusability, which is critical for future Nasa lunar landings. The 124-metre rocket is scheduled to launch from Starbase in Texas.
articles.description: The attempt follows an unsuccessful effort to catch of the rocket’s booster which instead came down in the ocean.

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV condemns Amazon deforestation and murders of Indigenous leaders
articles.title: Pope condemns murders of Peru’s Indigenous leaders, deforestation of Amazon
articles.summary: During his tour of South America, Pope Leo XIV met with Indigenous communities in the Peruvian city of Pucallpa to denounce the environmental destruction of the Amazon rainforest. The pontiff demanded justice for the dozens of Indigenous leaders killed while defending their territories from illegal mining and logging, while noting that the Peruvian Amazon lost approximately 200,000 hectares of natural forest in 2025.
articles.description: Pontiff says he supports Indigenous efforts to protect their lands, demands justice for slain environmental defenders.

articles.headline: Pope urges end to Amazon deforestation
articles.title: Pope urges end to Amazon deforestation
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV warns deforestation and illegal mining are threatening the Amazon rainforest and the local communities.

articles.headline: Apple launches health research study to evaluate conversational artificial intelligence tools
articles.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
articles.summary: Apple announced the Apple HealthAI Usage Study in collaboration with clinical platform OpenEvidence to evaluate how users interact with conversational medical tools. Seeking up to 200,000 United States participants aged 21 and older using an iPhone 15 Pro, the research aims to improve tool design and ensure responses remain accurate and understandable while protecting user confidentiality.
articles.description: Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical […]

articles.headline: Trump sidelines JD Vance from Iran file to focus on domestic issues
articles.title: How does Iran view shift in US approach after JD Vance ordered away?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump directed Vice President JD Vance to focus on domestic issues such as alleged Democratic corruption rather than ongoing negotiations with Tehran. Analysts suggest the move signals that reaching a deal with Iran is no longer a priority for Washington, potentially escalating regional conflict as maritime hostilities continue in the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing military blockades and severe sanctions.
articles.description: Washington believes maritime blockade, overland border disruptions, air restrictions and isolating sanctions are working

articles.headline: West Bengal police kill shooting suspect during an arrest attempt
articles.title: In latest ‘encounter’, West Bengal police kill a man accused of shooting at a constable two days ago
articles.summary: A man accused of shooting a police constable in West Bengal was killed in a gunfight with law enforcement on November 15, 2026. The suspect, Ratan Sheikh, was cornered at a brick kiln in Nanoor while evading arrest for allegedly injuring constable Biswajit Das two days prior. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari defended the police action, asserting that criminals have no place in the state.
articles.description: This is the fifth instance of an accused killed in police firing in West Bengal, within six months of the BJP coming to power in the State; this was an “extrajudicial execution”, says civil society group

articles.headline: Bangladesh clothing factories shut down as workers strike over minimum wage
articles.title: Clothing factories shut in Bangladesh as workers strike over pay
articles.summary: Nearly one hundred fifty garment production sites across industrial hubs in Savar, Ashulia, and Gazipur suspended operations after employees walked off the job demanding an increase to thirty thousand taka monthly. Protesters blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway before police intervention. Industry leaders warn that continued unrest threatens international supply chains for global brands like H&M and Zara.
articles.description: Workers are striking over demands for a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) a month.

articles.headline: Myanmar military airstrike kills twelve at displaced persons camp
articles.title: Myanmar airstrike on displaced persons camp kills 12, say witnesses
articles.summary: A military airstrike conducted by Myanmar forces killed twelve people at a camp for displaced persons in Rakhine State, according to witnesses and rescue workers. The attack on Friday destroyed bamboo housing in Ponnagyun township and injured eighteen others. Myanmar has faced continuous civil conflict since the military coup five years ago, leaving regions like Rakhine severely impacted by ongoing aerial bombardments and blockades.
articles.description: Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions

articles.headline: Leaked Rosstat data reveals at least 450,000 Russian war deaths
articles.title: Russian casualties ‘reach 450,000’: What that means for the Ukraine war
articles.summary: Leaked records from Russia's state statistics agency, Rosstat, indicate that at least 450,000 Russians died in the Ukraine conflict up to August. The files were obtained by hacking groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Ukraine's Silent Crow. Experts believe the data is authentic, revealing high casualty numbers among older men from minority regions and thousands of foreign fighters recruited through deceptive overseas advertisements.
articles.description: Leaked Russian records reveal a war toll that falls hardest on older men, poorer regions and foreign recruits.

articles.headline: Assam government announces nine lakh rupees ex gratia for minibus truck collision victims
articles.title: Family of each deceased in minibus-truck collision to get ₹9 lakh ex gratia: Assam CM
articles.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced an ex gratia payment of nine lakh rupees for the families of each person killed in a head-on collision between a minibus and a truck near Kaziranga National Park. Twenty-six people died in the accident on November 13, 2026. The state government is covering medical costs for the eighteen injured individuals currently receiving treatment at regional medical facilities.
articles.description: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said 26 people died in the head-on collision near Kaziranga National Park, and admitted some traffic restrictions had been relaxed “because of political pressure”

articles.headline: Guadalajara cartel founder Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies in hospital at age 80
articles.title: Founder of Guadalajara cartel dies in hospital after decades in prison
articles.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, who founded the Guadalajara cartel and was imprisoned since 1989 for crimes including the 1985 killing of a United States drug enforcement agent, has died at age 80 from multiple organ failure at a hospital in Guadalajara. Local security authorities confirmed his death after he was transferred from a maximum-security prison due to declining health.
articles.description: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo was convicted of the 1985 murder of a US drug enforcement agent and a Mexican pilot.

articles.headline: Sudanese Armed Forces capture al-Khuwai to counter Rapid Support Forces
articles.title: How SAF successes in Sudan’s Kordofan could turn tide against the RSF
articles.summary: The Sudanese Armed Forces gained control over al-Khuwai and other localities in West Kordofan, shifting the military balance against the Rapid Support Forces. The ongoing offensive has broken the siege on al-Obeid and opened new strategic supply routes. This territorial advance weakens the paramilitary group's tribal alliances and could reposition Darfur as the new epicentre of the prolonged nationwide conflict.
articles.description: The SAF successes in Kordofan are seeing the battle against the RSF turn in favour of the Sudanese government.

articles.headline: Ethiopia blames Egypt, Eritrea for Tigray attacks
articles.title: Ethiopia blames Egypt, Eritrea for Tigray attacks
articles.description: Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of leading TPLF attacks in Tigray, with Egypt providing logistical support.

articles.headline: Czechs rally against gov’t threat to media independence
articles.title: Czechs rally against gov’t threat to media independence
articles.description: Czechs rallied in Prague over plans to shift public media funding to the state, raising fears of government influence.

articles.headline: Russian billionaires quietly contemplate political future after Vladimir Putin's departure
articles.title: Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin
articles.summary: Some members of Russia's ultra-rich business elite are privately considering a post-Putin political landscape following decades of strict Kremlin control. According to analyst Arkady Ostrovsky, Western sanctions and domestic limitations have left tycoons with minimal political influence. Although President Vladimir Putin has served for twenty-five years, uncertainty remains over potential leadership succession and future economic conditions.
articles.description: Some Russian tycoons are pining after a return to a 1990s system of oligarchy, when businessmen enjoyed power

articles.headline: Libyan city of Derna undergoes rapid two billion dollar reconstruction
articles.title: Libyan town rebuilt after devastating floods becomes showcase for strongman's rule
articles.summary: Eastern Libya is utilizing a two billion dollar state-allocated fund to rapidly rebuild Derna following catastrophic floods in September 2023 that killed thousands. While many survivors have received free new housing in developments commissioned by Belkacem Haftar, international critics and rights groups have raised serious concerns regarding financial transparency, public accountability, and the absolute lack of published spending records.
articles.description: The remarkable reconstruction of Derna is being used as a showcase for the rest of Libya by Khalifa Haftar and his sons.

articles.headline: Astronomers discover unusual pair of distant quasars in the early universe
articles.title: Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified a strange pair of quasars located just 18,100 light-years apart when the universe was only 900 million years old. Officially designated as J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the discovery was studied using the James Webb Space Telescope and the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii, leaving scientists investigating how such massive black holes could have formed so early.
articles.description: Two celestial bodies—Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua—are a close pair of ancient quasars challenging ideas about early black hole growth

articles.headline: Zambia attracts billions in mining investments while local workers question benefits
articles.title: Zambia’s copper boom attracts billions in investment, but who benefits?
articles.summary: President Hakainde Hichilema announced that Zambia has secured over 12 billion dollars in mining investments since 2022 to expand copper production for the global energy transition. Major firms like First Quantum Minerals and International Resources Holding are driving the sector. However, trade unions report that local mineworkers have experienced no improvements in employment conditions amid rising operational costs.
articles.description: Workers' rights, environmental concerns and local businesses remain at the centre of the debate.

articles.headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang departs company following recent controversies
articles.title: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia Corporation Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has left the company he cofounded thirty-three years ago after facing allegations regarding chip smuggling scandals and extramarital affairs. Industry analysts note that while Huang served as a central visionary figure for the artificial intelligence hardware market, the company's product roadmap and manufacturing plans remain locked in through 2027 despite his sudden departure.
articles.description: On January 6th, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got his rockstar moment at last. He strode triumphantly onstage, hand raised in the air, to the claps and cheers of a 14,000-person arena absolutely packed with influencers and fans, their faces awash in blue glow, as he made his entrance in a black leather jacket that […]

articles.headline: Indian external intelligence agency linked to overseas operations targeting separatists
articles.title: Will R&AW’s overseas operations affect ties? | Explained
articles.summary: India's external intelligence agency, the Research and Analysis Wing, faced international scrutiny following allegations from the United States, Canada, Australia, and Pakistan regarding operations targeting Khalistani separatist operatives. According to a Washington Post report, American officials claim former agency chief Samant Goel approved a foiled assassination plot against U.S. and Canadian citizen Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
articles.description: Why have the U.S., Canada, Australia and Pakistan brought up allegations that the agency has spearheaded targeted killings and surveillance of separatists on their soil? What is the Indian government’s stand? Do these operations follow certain norms, especially if it’s a friendly country?

articles.headline: Mirra Andreeva wins WTA Finals title after defeating Elina Svitolina in Indian Wells
articles.title: Teenager Andreeva caps stunning week with WTA Finals title
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old tennis player Mirra Andreeva defeated Elina Svitolina in straight sets to capture the WTA Finals singles championship in California. The Russian competitor did not drop a single set throughout the tournament, securing two million five hundred fifty thousand pounds in prize money alongside a custom vehicle. Following this victory, Andreeva rose to second place in the world rankings.
articles.description: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva caps her stellar season with a hard-fought victory over Elina Svitolina to win the WTA Finals.

articles.headline: Thirteen-year-old boy confirmed as fourth Indian fatality in UAE crash
articles.title: 13-year-old boy identified as fourth Indian killed in UAE road accident
articles.summary: A 13-year-old boy from Gujarat named Aatif Mohmmed Imran Mansur was identified by authorities as the fourth Indian killed in a massive 23-vehicle road accident in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, on November 12, 2026. According to the UAE Ministry of Interior, the disaster left 14 people dead and 30 injured, including the boy's parents and sister who received hospital treatment.
articles.description: The accident involved 23 vehicles, including trucks, and left 30 people injured

articles.headline: Bangladesh seeks extradition of ousted leader Sheikh Hasina from India
articles.title: What are the legal compulsions and political hurdles in Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh? | Explained
articles.summary: Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir announced that Bangladesh is seeking the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner transfer process after she applied for a new passport and national identity card in Dhaka on November 9, 2026. Hasina has been living in India since August 5, 2024, following a student-led uprising, and faces a death sentence by the International Crimes Tribunal for a deadly police crackdown.
articles.description: Sheikh Hasina wants to return to Bangladesh as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024, and the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka has sentenced her to death for it

articles.headline: Ukraine and Russia develop military satellite networks amid communication reliance concerns
articles.title: Ukraine, Russia race to build military satellite networks as war rages on
articles.summary: Ukraine is exploring alternative satellite networks through partnerships with Danish, Finnish, and domestic companies to reduce its heavy reliance on SpaceX and Starlink. Following recent speed limitations imposed on Ukrainian military communications and drone operations by billionaire Elon Musk, Kyiv aims to build sovereign capabilities while Russia simultaneously attempts to develop its own Rassvet satellite constellation.
articles.description: Kyiv seeks to break reliance on Starlink as Moscow develops its own satellite constellation for military communications.

articles.headline: Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision
articles.title: Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision, says NTSB
articles.summary: An asphalt cargo vessel experienced a steering casualty before striking a docked riverboat on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday, according to National Transportation Safety Board findings released on Sunday. The collision injured 32 people from the American Heritage riverboat, which carried 129 passengers and listed before tipping onto its side.
articles.description: Preliminary findings by National Transportation Safety Board investigators suggest the tanker suffered a "steering casualty" before colliding with the cruise ship on Friday.

articles.headline: England defeat Spain to claim top spot in UEFA Nations League
articles.title: England stun Spain to end La Roja’s 43-game unbeaten run
articles.summary: England secured a dramatic victory against Spain in Madrid on November 16, 2026, finishing first in Group A3 on goal difference despite playing with ten men following Elliott Anderson's red card. Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White scored for the visitors before Nico Williams and Mikel Oyarzabal responded for the hosts in a tense finish.
articles.description: Spain suffer first defeat since March 2024 after losing 3-2 to England in Madrid despite grandstand finish.

articles.headline: U.S. court permits Khalistani separatist to serve summons on Indian officials
articles.title: Can India refuse to serve summons in the Pannun case?
articles.summary: A United States court permitted Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to serve summons on National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Kumar Goel through Indian courts. The civil lawsuit alleges a conspiracy to assassinate Pannun, linking to Federal Bureau of Investigation findings from June 2023, according to court documents published in November 2026.
articles.description: A U.S. court has allowed Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to pursue serving summons on National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former RAW chief Samant Goel through Indian courts. The order raises several legal questions

articles.headline: Paris police ban demonstrations near educational institutions amid ongoing protests
articles.title: Police ban protests near 10 schools and five universities in Paris
articles.summary: Paris police issued a five-day ban on protests near 10 secondary schools and five universities from November 16 to 20, 2026. Paris police chief Patrice Faure cited persistent violence and blockades that damaged public property and injured educational staff. Authorities reported that 1,548 people have been arrested in Paris since demonstrations began in September.
articles.description: The order will be in place from 16 to 20 November, Paris police chief Patrice Faure says.

articles.headline: Yemen’s Houthis unilaterally release 600 war detainees
articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis unilaterally release 600 war detainees
articles.description: Yemen’s Houthis have released 600 people imprisoned during the country’s civil war.

articles.headline: Thousands of Czech protesters rally against public media funding changes
articles.title: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
articles.summary: Thousands of Czech citizens gathered in Prague on Sunday to protest government plans to replace public media license fees with state budget funding. Organisers from the Million Moments for Democracy association estimated attendance at roughly 400,000 people. Critics argue the legislation threatens media freedom, while the coalition government led by Prime Minister Andrej Babis insists editorial independence will remain unaffected.
articles.description: Protesters say the move will stifle media freedom, while the government insists broadcasters need to cut costs.

articles.headline: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after alleged arson attack
articles.title: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after alleged arson attack
articles.description: Estonia is closing its border crossings with Russia following an alleged arson attempt at a drone factory.

articles.headline: Bilkis Bano reflects on her life struggle at Kochi women conference
articles.title: My entire life has been a struggle, says Bilkis Bano at GIO conference in Kochi
articles.summary: Gujarat riots survivor Bilkis Bano stated that her entire existence has been a struggle while inaugurating the International Conference on Women in Kochi on November 15, 2026. Speaking at the event organized by the Girls Islamic Organisation, she reflected on her prolonged legal battle for justice following the 2002 riots where she was gang-raped and lost seven family members, highlighting an ongoing journey that her husband Patel Yakub Rasool noted involved multiple relocations and denied rights.
articles.description: Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage.

articles.headline: West Bengal BJP chief warns Christian missionary schools over conversions
articles.title: West Bengal BJP president alleges conversions at missionary schools; draws flak
articles.summary: West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party chief Samik Bhattacharya warned Christian missionary schools on November 15, 2026, alleging religious conversions and anti-India activities. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba urged him to publicly name the institutions. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari accused the previous government of exclusively recognizing Muslims as a minority, asserting that Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains also qualify.
articles.description: This is the first time a senior State BJP leader has made remarks about the community, even as Christian groups have protested against attacks on churches

articles.headline: Traditional Kashmiri wazwan feasts linked to rising diabetes cases
articles.title: As diabetes spikes in Kashmir, the health lens turns to the fabled wazwan
articles.summary: High-calorie Kashmiri wazwan feasts are a key cultural factor driving a sharp rise in diabetes across Jammu and Kashmir, according to experts and a new book released on November 14, 2026. Ministry data indicates millions were screened, adding over two lakh new patients in three years. Authors attributed the surge to sedentary winters, rice-centric meals, and rapid urbanization.
articles.description: Subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living has been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns persist largely unchanged, the doctor-authors of Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir say

articles.headline: Centre sanctions new infrastructure along China border in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: Why has Centre sanctioned fresh infrastructure along the China border in Arunachal Pradesh? | Explained
articles.summary: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police has sanctioned new infrastructure construction in Arunachal Pradesh amid ongoing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control since late July. This follows the February approval by the Cabinet Committee on Security for the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads project to build twenty-six roads.
articles.description: The tension in Arunachal Pradesh has persisted even though India and China held three high-level border talks since July 2026

articles.headline: Assam accident autopsy scheduled as chief minister visits victims
articles.title: Assam accident: Autopsy of 26 bodies on November 14; CM to visit injured, meet families of deceased
articles.summary: Authorities in Assam announced that autopsies for twenty-six individuals killed in a vehicle collision on November 13, 2026, will occur on November 14 at Swahid Kushal Konwar Civil Hospital in Golaghat. Minister Ranoj Pegu stated that seven critically injured patients remain in the intensive care unit at Jorhat Medical College Hospital. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma plans to visit affected families in Golaghat district.
articles.description: Twenty-six people died in a head-on collision between the two vehicles at Rangajan on National Highway 715 near Kaziranga National Park on November 13

articles.headline: Israeli drone filmed flying low outside homes in southern Lebanon
articles.title: Israeli drone filmed flying low outside homes in southern Lebanon
articles.description: Video shows an Israeli drone flying at low altitude over a residential area in southern Lebanon.

articles.headline: Hyderabad hospital performs combined heart valve procedures on elderly patient
articles.title: Hyderabad hospital performs combined heart valve procedures in single sitting
articles.summary: Cardiologists at Apollo Hospitals in Hyderabad successfully performed Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Balloon Mitral Valvotomy on an 83-year-old patient in a single sitting. The minimally invasive procedure was demonstrated during the Hyderabad Valves 2026 conference, which brings together international heart specialists for live case demonstrations and advanced medical discussions.

articles.headline: Southeast Asian leaders gather for summit amid United States trade disruptions
articles.title: Southeast Asian leaders to meet as Trump visit highlights trade disruption
articles.summary: Association of Southeast Asian Nations leaders are meeting in Manila, Philippines, from November 15 to 17, 2026, as United States President Donald Trump undertakes an Asia Pacific tour featuring trade talks and a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trade policy experts note that despite increased regional exports driven by electronics, leaders remain concerned about potential future sectoral tariffs and restrictive trade measures.
articles.description: ASEAN summit comes as US president embarks on Asia trip that will see him meet China's Xi.

articles.headline: Prince Harry visits Ukraine to meet Invictus Games hopefuls
articles.title: Prince Harry in Ukraine meeting Invictus 2027 hopefuls
articles.summary: British Prince Harry made a surprise visit to Lviv, Ukraine, on Saturday, meeting wounded combat veterans and medics at a clinic specialising in war rehabilitation. The 42-year-old royal watched wheelchair rugby players trying out for Ukraine's largest ever team for the upcoming Invictus Games. He founded the Invictus Games Foundation in 2014 to support recovering military personnel through adaptive sports programmes.
articles.description: British royal says he's 'taken a risk' in his fourth surprise visit to Ukraine since 2022 to meet wounded veterans.

articles.headline: India secures Twenty20 International series victory against New Zealand
articles.title: Batting a worry as rookie pacers script rare triumph
articles.summary: The Indian cricket team claimed a 3-0 lead in its five-match Twenty20 International series against New Zealand within the first week of arriving in the country. The dominant victories were primarily driven by the visiting batting lineup on bowler-friendly surfaces during the tour, according to recent sports reports published on November 16, 2026.
articles.description: The lack of conviction from the Indian batters almost takes the sheen away from the ODI series win ahead of the Tests

articles.headline: Yemeni city faces severe health crisis amid Houthi blockade
articles.title: Siege fuels disease fears in Yemen’s Taiz
articles.summary: The ongoing Houthi blockade in Taiz, Yemen, has triggered acute shortages of food, safe water, and medical supplies, severely restricting civilian access to hospitals. According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, thousands of residents suffer from acute watery diarrhoea and suspected cholera as waste accumulates and sanitation trucks are blocked from reaching local landfills.
articles.description: Health officials warn that falling numbers of recorded infections may conceal a worsening disease crisis in Taiz.

articles.headline: Christian priest says US denied him a visa for being Palestinian
articles.title: Christian priest says US denied him a visa for being Palestinian
articles.description: A Christian priest from Bethlehem, the birthplace of Jesus, says the US denied him a visa because he is Palestinian.

articles.headline: Arjun Erigaisi catches Maxime Vachier-Lagrave at top of Group D
articles.title: Arjun finds form, snaps Vachier-Lagrave’s winning run
articles.summary: Arjun Erigaisi defeated Maxime Vachier-Lagrave in their second game on Saturday in Budapest, handing the French chess player his first Fast Classic defeat at the Total Chess World Championship Tour. The Indian player caught Vachier-Lagrave and Hans Niemann at the top of Group D with 13 points each. Meanwhile, Magnus Carlsen drew both matches against Shakhriyar Mamedyarov, ending his chances of finishing first in Group C.

articles.headline: FAA ground stop disrupts NBA, NHL and college football weekend travel
articles.title: US air travel thrown into chaos after nationwide ground stop halts flights
articles.summary: More than 1.5 million air passengers and multiple sports teams faced travel chaos after the United States Federal Aviation Administration halted departing flights nationwide for over four hours due to a telecommunications outage. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated it will take time to restore capacity following the incident, which caused thousands of delays and cancellations before the ground stop was lifted at 8:15pm Eastern time on Friday.
articles.description: More than 1.5 million passengers face travel disruption as domestic and international airlines warn of knock-on delays.

articles.title: Nearly 1,500 migrants reach Spain’s Canary Islands in one day

articles.headline: Morocco enters FIFA top five men rankings after strong performances
articles.title: Morocco becomes first Arab nation in FIFA’s top five men’s rankings
articles.summary: Morocco have entered FIFA's top five men's team rankings for the first time, becoming the first Arab country to achieve the milestone. The Atlas Lions moved up two spots on Sunday, surpassing Brazil and Portugal following strong continental performances. Mohamed Ouhabi's squad recently maintained a 100 percent record in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying by defeating Niger 5-0 in Rabat.
articles.description: Morocco moved past former Euro champions Portugal and record World Cup winners Brazil to achieve its best FIFA ranking.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces redeploy from Bab al-Mandeb to defend Aden
articles.title: Yemeni government forces redeploy from Bab al-Mandeb to defend Aden
articles.summary: Forces allied with Yemen's internationally recognised government are withdrawing from territory near the Bab al-Mandeb strait to defend the interim capital of Aden from the Houthi armed group. A Southern Armed Forces spokesman stated on Sunday that troops are leaving Dhubab airport to reinforce front lines. The move follows recent Houthi advances and aims to address escalating security threats across southwestern governorates.
articles.description: Spokesman for the Southern Armed Forces says group is repositioning from Dhubab airport and areas around Bab al-Mandeb.

articles.headline: Spain reports nearly 2200 migrant arrivals in Canary Islands
articles.title: Nearly 2,200 migrants reach Canary Islands in two days, Spain says
articles.summary: Authorities in Madrid recorded the influx over a forty-eight hour period via maritime rescue operations. According to the Spanish maritime rescue service on November 15, 2026, personnel assisted 1324 individuals on fourteen vessels, primarily reaching El Hierro. The Interior Ministry stated that over 13000 of the 28000 sea arrivals between January and October landed in the archipelago, prompting a migration emergency declaration on November 11, 2026.
articles.description: Spain declared a migration emergency on the islands on November 11 following a rise in arrivals in recent weeks, particularly from sub-Saharan Africa

articles.headline: Supreme Court reviews Digital News Publishers Association plea over DPDP Act
articles.title: Privacy vs press freedom: where should the line be drawn?
articles.summary: The Digital News Publishers Association, representing 21 news publishers, petitioned the Supreme Court on October 27, 2026, to request an interim stay on the Digital Personal Data Protection Act of 2023. Represented by senior advocate Madhavi Divan, the association argued that the legislation lacks a specific journalistic exemption, which threatens press freedom and investigative reporting.
articles.description: The DPDP Act, 2023, has reignited the debate over privacy and press freedom. How does the law reconcile data protection with the public’s right to know?

articles.headline: Somalia credits international community for progress amid ongoing challenges
articles.title: Somalia: We would not have recovered without the international community
articles.summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar stated that the nation achieved significant recovery following decades of civil war. The United Nations previously maintained a political office until its conclusion in October at government request. Officials currently confront an al-Shabaab insurgency while African Union peacekeepers remain deployed, though funding reductions threaten the mission and domestic political disputes persist regarding presidential legitimacy.
articles.description: Somalia continues to face al-Shabab rebellion and political friction, leading officials to urge international support.

articles.headline: Germany parliament approves expanded operational powers for intelligence agencies
articles.title: German spies granted sweeping new powers
articles.summary: The German Bundestag passed legislation on November 13, 2026, granting the foreign intelligence agency BND and domestic service BfV powers to actively disrupt cyberattacks and hack adversaries. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt supported the reform to counter foreign espionage, while opposition party Die Linke criticized potential privacy violations and historical parallels to East Germany's Stasi.
articles.description: Parliament passes legislation months after a thwarted attack at Leipzig-Halle airport, which Berlin linked to Russia.

articles.headline: Expert urges India and Bangladesh leadership to renew Ganga Water Treaty
articles.title: India, Bangladesh leaderships should support temporary renewal of Ganga Water Treaty, says expert
articles.summary: Manjur Ahmed Chowdhury stated that insufficient time remains to fully revise the thirty-year-old Ganga Water Treaty before its expiration in four weeks. The former chairman recommended a temporary renewal for three to five years requiring high-level political approval from India and Bangladesh. Without a binding agreement, Bangladesh faces severe risks to its upcoming agricultural season and overall economic stability.
articles.description: Full revision of the Ganga Water Treaty is not possible in the four weeks left before it expires, says Manjur Ahmed Chowdhury, former Chairman of the National River Conservation Commission of Bangladesh, but ‘having a bad treaty is better than not having any treaty at all’

articles.headline: Tens of thousands protest in Prague against public media reforms
articles.title: Thousands rally in Czech Republic against state media funding changes
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of demonstrators assembled in Letna Park in Prague on Sunday to oppose government proposals altering public service media funding. Prime Minister Andrej Babis aims to replace household fees with state budget financing, a move opponents claim will compromise broadcaster independence. The legislation, which has passed a preliminary parliamentary vote, has drawn sharp criticism from international press freedom organizations.
articles.description: Critics say proposed funding changes will give the government more control of state media.

articles.headline: BJP worker killed in West Bengal amid intra-party feud suspicions
articles.title: Murder of BJP worker by own party members sparks speculation of intra-party feud in West Bengal
articles.summary: An active Bharatiya Janata Party worker died on November 15, 2026, after sustaining injuries during a scuffle in Panihati, West Bengal, prompting local allegations of an internal feud involving former Trinamool Congress members. The altercation followed protests over a beaten businessman, drawing claims from local leaders that recently switched members caused the violence. Meanwhile, similar factional tensions emerged in Barrackpore against a local MLA.
articles.description: Since the BJP came to power in the summer of 2026, allegations that differences persist between supporters of the party who joined the BJP before their assembly poll victory and those who came after have surfaced frequently.

articles.headline: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reports Q2 net loss of Rs 5,531 crore
articles.title: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reports Q2 net loss of ₹5,531 crore
articles.summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,531 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by a one-time exceptional charge of Rs 6,738 crore and Jaguar Land Rover restructuring. Despite the loss, overall revenue rose thirty-five percent year-over-year to Rs 96,340 crore, supported by record domestic sales exceeding 200,000 units.
articles.description: The figures are not comparable because last year the company had exceptional gains due to the demerger of the company. During the period, the company’s revenue increased to ₹96,340 crore from ₹71,414 crore in the year ago period, up 35% YoY

articles.headline: Narendra Modi says tribal communities suffered most due to Maoist violence
articles.title: ‘Escaping extreme poverty and Naxalism has improved tribal lives’, says PM Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed a tribal pride programme in Gadchiroli, stating that tribal populations suffered severely and lost voting rights under previous administrations due to Maoist violence. He highlighted recent developmental initiatives, including the inauguration and foundation laying of projects worth approximately 30000 crore rupees across multiple states.
articles.description: PM cites World Bank report to claim that 50 crore Indians have escaped extreme poverty over last 12 to 13 years; says 125 districts were Naxal-affected in 2014, as previous regimes closed their eyes to the problem

articles.headline: UN says Israeli policies worsened deadly impact of Gaza winter storm
articles.title: UN says Israeli policies worsened deadly impact of Gaza winter storm
articles.description: The UN says Israel could have prevented death and destruction caused by the storm in Gaza had it allowed sufficient aid.

articles.headline: Hundreds of thousands protest Czech public media funding changes
articles.title: Czechs gather in big numbers to reject government's plan to overhaul funding of public media
articles.summary: Massive crowds rallied at Prague's Letná Park on November 15, 2026, to denounce Prime Minister Andrej Babis and his coalition's plan to overhaul public broadcaster funding, which critics warn threatens media freedom. According to lead organizer Mikulas Minar from the Million Moments for Democracy group, approximately 350,000 demonstrators attended. The controversial legislation would replace license fees with state budget funding and reduce budgets by fifteen percent.
articles.description: The massive protest took place at the capital's Letná Park, where huge crowds gathered during the 1989 Velvet Revolution, which ended more than 40 years of communist rule in the country

articles.headline: Judge halts Trump administration closure of Washington DC golf course
articles.title: Judge blocks Trump closure of 'Trash Island' Washington DC golf course on Sunday
articles.summary: US District Judge Ana Reyes issued a temporary restraining order preventing the federal government from closing the historic East Potomac Golf Links in Washington DC for renovations. Reyes ruled that the administration violated federal laws to meet an arbitrary deadline and acted in bad faith, scheduling the order to remain in effect until November 28 while legal proceedings continue.
articles.description: The temporary order is part of a months-long challenge to the US president's plans to upgrade East Potomac Golf Links into a championship course.

articles.headline: Brinda Karat criticizes Modi government over agricultural and corporate policies
articles.title: Modi govt. implementing policies to hand over agri sector to corporates: Brinda Karat
articles.summary: Communist Party of India Marxist leader Brinda Karat accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration on November 15, 2026, of enacting policies that surrender the agricultural sector to domestic and foreign corporate entities. Speaking at the thirty sixth All India Kisan Sabha meeting in Nalgonda, she criticized soaring commodity prices, land acquisitions displacing indigenous Adivasi communities, and agreements with the United States that harm farmers, while urging Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy to protect constitutional rights.
articles.description: Centre systemically weakening Constitution and its institutions, she alleged

articles.headline: Uniform sugarcane pricing is impractical for factories, says Satish Jarkiholi
articles.title: All sugar factories cannot pay same price to farmers, says Satish Jarkiholi
articles.summary: Karnataka sugar factory owner and minister Satish Jarkiholi stated that uniform sugarcane pricing is impractical due to varying financial health, crop quality, and sugar recovery rates among factories. Speaking in Belagavi, he noted that base prices were set at 3,600 rupees per tonne following discussions with farmers, while urging the Union government to increase the minimum selling price of sugar.
articles.description: Union government should revise Minimum Selling Price of sugar, according to the Minister

articles.headline: Revanth Reddy urges Prime Minister Modi to expedite Telangana irrigation projects
articles.title: Revanth urges Modi to expedite clearances for Telangana irrigation projects
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi to request assistance in resolving inter-State water disputes and securing pending clearances for regional irrigation projects. The Chief Minister sought Maharashtra's consent for the Tummidihatti project and requested an additional 5,000 billion rupees under a special capital investment scheme to complete near-finished infrastructure developments.
articles.description: Seeks Centre’s intervention to secure Maharashtra’s approval for Tummidihatti project; requests ₹5,000 crore under SASCI; invites PM to Khelo India Youth Games

articles.headline: Leaders demand probe into deaths of two special police officers
articles.title: Congress demands probe into two SPOs’ death in Kishtwar; BJP claims their remains were ‘dishonoured’
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir political parties demanded an investigation on November 15, 2026, into the circumstances surrounding the deaths of Special Police Officers Babi Chand and Rashpal Kumar in Kishtwar. While opposition leaders questioned whether the officers were mistakenly shot by the Army or targeted by militants, the Bharatiya Janata Party alleged that the bodies were treated disrespectfully during transport, prompting demands for a comprehensive inquiry into the incident and subsequent police strategy.
articles.description: Political parties raise questions about the death of the two men on November 12, with the J&K Police having not yet issued a statement on the matter

articles.headline: Flames engulf Syrian refugee camp in eastern Lebanon
articles.title: Flames engulf Syrian refugee camp in eastern Lebanon
articles.description: A fire tore through a Syrian refugee camp in Bar Elias, eastern Lebanon.

articles.headline: South Eastern Railway probes empty Vande Bharat train journey with faulty brakes
articles.title: Empty Vande Bharat train travels 463 km with faulty brakes in Ranchi division
articles.summary: The South Eastern Railway zone initiated an investigation after an empty Vande Bharat train travelled 463 km from Jharkhand to Uttar Pradesh with isolated braking systems. Railway staff and crew members allegedly ignored multiple warnings from loco pilots regarding poor brake performance before the issue was identified at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station. Officials cited widespread staff negligence during the October journey.
articles.description: Railway staff allegedly failed to ensure proper integration of the Vande Bharat's braking system with that of the goods locomotive which was to pull the rake through out the journey

articles.headline: BJP leader demands apology from Rahul Gandhi over Bharat Summit
articles.title: BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of treason over Bharat Summit
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party Telangana president N. Ramchander Rao demanded an unconditional apology from opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on November 15, 2026, accusing him of treason and inviting foreign anti-national groups to the Bharat Summit. Rao claimed the event allowed foreign interference in internal political affairs and defended the cancellation of a foreign journalist visa, while a union minister questioned the event expenditure.

articles.headline: CRPF withdraws anti-Naxal battalion from Chhattisgarh to deploy in Manipur
articles.title: CRPF withdraws anti-Naxal battalion from Chhattisgarh for Manipur duties
articles.summary: The Central Reserve Police Force withdrew more than one thousand personnel from anti-Naxal operations in Sukma district to bolster security forces in Manipur, marking the first such de-induction since the government declared the end of armed Maoism. Local police warned the move creates an operational vacuum, though officials stated similar troop reassignments may follow to strengthen regional borders.
articles.description: A battalion of more than 1,000 personnel based in Sukma has been sent to Manipur, with a proposal to withdraw at least three more from Chhattisgarh and Odisha, officials told PTI

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister urges central team to submit cyclone report
articles.title: Cyclone damage: Andhra Pradesh CM urges Central team to submit report in 10 days; State puts total loss at ₹2,484 crore
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu urged a central inspection team led by Chittaranjan Das to submit its assessment report within ten days and release immediate financial assistance following Cyclone Murasu. State assessments placed total losses at ₹2,484.43 crore across multiple sectors, prompting calls for permanent infrastructure solutions and targeted relief for affected agricultural communities.

articles.headline: Defence minister urges adoption of advanced technologies in non-destructive testing
articles.title: Rajnath Singh calls for AI, robotics in Non-Destructive Testing to strengthen defence sector
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged professionals on November 15, 2026, to adopt artificial intelligence, machine learning, and robotics in non-destructive testing to enhance India's defence ecosystem and achieve strategic self-reliance. Addressing a conference in Hyderabad, he emphasized that indigenous systems must meet strict reliability standards and called for domestic solutions tailored to national industrial requirements.

articles.headline: Rajnath Singh calls for indigenous development of advanced inspection technologies
articles.title: India should become innovator, global leader in advanced tech: Rajnath Singh
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged India to transition from a technology user to a global leader in non-destructive testing and aerospace evaluation during a conference in Hyderabad on November 15, 2026. He stressed that stringent quality assurance and indigenous development of advanced sensors and artificial intelligence are essential for securing defense supply chains and ensuring operational reliability.
articles.description: Defence Minister calls for strengthening India’s indigenous Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) capabilities

articles.headline: Tanker ship collides with docked river cruise boat in New Orleans
articles.title: All passengers, crew on New Orleans cruise ship survive crash with tanker on Mississippi River
articles.summary: A tanker vessel collided with the river cruise boat American Heritage while it was docked near the port of New Orleans on Friday. The collision involved approximately 130 passengers on board and left the pleasure vessel partially submerged and listing. Local emergency services responded with rescue operations, though the precise cause of the collision and the extent of any injuries remained unclear immediately.
articles.description: Tanker owned by subsidiary of Chinese shipbuilder; too early to tell what might have caused the crash, but videos indicate some kind of catastrophic system failure on the vessel, a maritime law expert said
